description: Formalize Goldbach's conjecture in Lean 4. Prove the conjecture holds for all even n ≤ 10^6 computationally, formalize Vinogradov's theorem (every sufficiently large odd number is the sum of three primes), and construct the Hardy-Littlewood circle method framework for additive problems. Deliver a working Lean verification tactic.

description: Prove that the rank of an elliptic curve equals the order of vanishing of its L-function at s=1. Formalize the BSD formula including the regulator, Tate-Shafarevich group, and Tamagawa numbers.

description: Prove that there are infinitely many pairs of primes differing by 2. Formalize Zhang's bounded gaps result and Maynard-Tao improvements. Explore connections to the Hardy-Littlewood conjecture and sieve theory.

description: Formalize global existence and uniqueness for 2D Navier-Stokes (Ladyzhenskaya's theorem). Prove the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg partial regularity theorem in 3D: the singular set has 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure zero. Formalize energy inequalities.

description: Prove Hironaka's resolution of singularities theorem for varieties in characteristic p > 0. Formalize known results for dimensions ≤ 3.

title: Catalan's Conjecture Generalizations

description: Compute and formalize π_n(S^m) for small n, m. Prove π_3(S^2) ≅ ℤ via the Hopf fibration. Construct the Hopf invariant and prove it detects the generator. Formalize the long exact sequence of a fibration.

title: Sierpiński Numbers: Covering Systems

title: Quadratic Reciprocity: Five Proofs Formalized

Show that the structure sheaf of a tropical scheme satisfies the tropical gluing axiom. Connect to the Grothendieck scheme-theoretic approach to tropical geometry.

title: Hilbert 12: Kronecker-Weber Generalization

title: Kaplansky's Conjectures

title: Random Matrices: Edge Universality

title: Representation Theory: Character Tables of S_n

title: Knot Invariants: Jones Polynomial Formalization

description: Formalize the Kantorovich optimal transport problem. Prove existence of optimal transport maps (Brenier's theorem for quadratic cost). Formalize Wasserstein distances and prove the Wasserstein GAN convergence properties.
title: Optimal Transport and Wasserstein Distances

description: Formalize BCH and Reed-Solomon codes over finite fields. Prove the BCH bound on minimum distance. Construct the Berlekamp-Massey decoding algorithm and prove correctness. Apply to concrete error-correction scenarios.
title: Algebraic Coding Theory: BCH and Reed-Solomon

description: Formalize the consistency of quantum field theory as a proof-theoretic question. Prove that if a physical theory T is consistent, then Con(T) is independent of PA. Show that physical consistency implies mathematical consistency but not vice versa.
title: Logic-Physics Bridge: Consistency of Physical Theories

description: Prove or disprove that every bounded linear operator on a separable Hilbert space has a non-trivial closed invariant subspace. Formalize known results for compact operators and normal operators.
title: Invariant Subspace Problem

description: Prove that Wall-Sun-Sun primes exist (primes p where p² divides F_{p-(p|5)}). Formalize the connection to Fermat's Last Theorem and establish search bounds for the first such prime.
title: Wall-Sun-Sun Primes

description: Prove that the connective constant for the self-avoiding walk on Z² equals (2+√2)/2 or determine its exact value. Formalize the Hara-Slade result and Nienhuis's conjecture.
title: Self-Avoiding Walk: Connective Constant

description: Prove the invariant subspace theorem for compact operators on Hilbert spaces (Aronszajn-Smith). Formalize Lomonosov's theorem: operators commuting with a nonzero compact operator have invariant subspaces. Explore the Enflo-Read counterexample structure.
title: Invariant Subspace Problem: Special Cases

description: Formalize the untyped lambda calculus. Prove the Church-Rosser theorem (confluence). Formalize the simply-typed lambda calculus and prove strong normalization. Construct the Böhm tree for undecidability of equivalence.
title: Lambda Calculus: Church-Rosser and Normalization

description: Formalize the PAC-Bayes framework in Lean 4. Prove the Catoni bound and McAllester bound. Apply to neural networks via Gaussian perturbation priors. Prove that PAC-Bayes bounds are asymptotically tight for linear classifiers.
title: PAC-Bayes Generalization Bounds

description: Formalize the Fisher information metric on parametric statistical models. Prove the Cramér-Rao bound as a geometric statement. Construct the alpha-connections and prove the dually flat structure. Apply to exponential families.
title: Information Geometry: Fisher Metric on Statistical Models

description: The Riemann zeta function zeta(s) has non-trivial zeros at s = 1/2 + i*gamma_n on the critical line (assuming RH). These zeros encode deep arithmetic information. Conjecture: the zeros gamma_n are the spectrum of a self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space, and this operator is the Casimir element of a quantum group G_q. Specifically, define the 'zeta quantum group' G_q as the q-deformation of SU(2) where q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1} (using the first zero gamma_1 ~ 14.13). The Casimir element C_q of G_q has eigenvalues that are quadratic functions of the representation labels, and the spectrum of C_q is {n(n+1) : n in N}. Conjecture: the Riemann zeros gamma_n are related to the spectrum of C_q by gamma_n = f(spectrum(C_q)) for some function f. If f is linear, this would mean the zeros are evenly spaced, which is false (the zeros have Poisson-like spacings). If f is logarithmic, gamma_n ~ pi*n/log(n) which matches the average spacing. Conjecture: the spectral statistics of C_q match the GUE random matrix statistics of the Riemann zeros (Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture). Test: compute the spectrum of C_q for G_q with q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1} and compare the spectral statistics with the Riemann zeros. Impact: the Riemann hypothesis is a representation-theoretic statement about quantum groups.
proof_strategy: Define the quantum group SU_q(2) with q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1} where gamma_1 ~ 14.13 is the first Riemann zero. The representation theory: irreducible representations V_n of dimension n+1 for n = 0, 1, 2, .... The Casimir element C_q acts on V_n with eigenvalue [n]_q * [n+1]_q where [m]_q = (q^m - q^{-m})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-integer. For q = e^{2*pi*i*gamma_1}: [m]_q = sin(m * pi * gamma_1) / sin(pi * gamma_1). The eigenvalues of C_q on V_n are: lambda_n = [n]_q * [n+1]_q = sin(n*pi*gamma_1) * sin((n+1)*pi*gamma_1) / sin(pi*gamma_1)^2. Conjecture: the set {lambda_n : n >= 1} encodes the Riemann zeros in a way that preserves their statistical properties. Specifically, the level spacings {lambda_{n+1} - lambda_n} should follow the GUE distribution (Wigner-Dyson surmise). Test: compute lambda_n for n = 1..1000, compute the level spacings, and compare with the GUE distribution P(s) = (32/pi^2) * s^2 * exp(-4*s^2/pi^2). Also compare with the Riemann zero spacings. This requires numerical computation of q-deformed representations.
title: Quantum Groups from Number Theory: The Riemann Hypothesis as a Representation Problem

description: Determine which integers can be represented as a sum of three cubes. Formalize known computational results and the density conjecture. Connect to the geometry of cubic surfaces and the Hasse principle.

description: Prove that if a polynomial map F: Cⁿ → Cⁿ has constant non-zero Jacobian determinant, then F is invertible. Formalize the reduction to degree 3 and connect to the Dixmier conjecture.

description: Prove that the union of k k-uniform intersecting hypergraphs has chromatic number at most k. Formalize the linear hypergraph version and recent probabilistic approaches.
title: Erdős-Faber-Lovász Conjecture

description: Formalize the discrete Fourier transform as representation theory of cyclic groups. Prove Parseval's theorem and the convolution theorem. Extend to arbitrary finite abelian groups. Prove the uncertainty principle: supp(f) · supp(f̂) ≥ |G|.

description: Solve the happy end problem for arbitrary n: determine the minimum number of points in general position in the plane that guarantee a convex n-gon. Formalize the Erdős–Szekeres theorem and improve known bounds.
title: Happy End Problem

description: Prove that the Euler-Mascheroni constant γ ≈ 0.5772 is irrational (or transcendental). Formalize continued fraction expansions and connect to the theory of special values of L-functions.

description: Determine all integer solutions to n! + 1 = m². Only three solutions are known (n=4,5,7). Formalize the connection to the ABC conjecture and explore bounds on the spacing between Brown numbers.

description: Prove that every graph on at least 3 vertices is determined up to isomorphism by its deck of vertex-deleted subgraphs. Formalize Kelly's lemma and prove for specific graph classes.

description: Formalize quaternion algebras and their classification over number fields. Prove the isomorphism between unit quaternions and SO(3). Construct the Cayley-Dickson construction and prove properties of octonions. Apply to gimbal lock avoidance in 3D rotation.

description: For every gentle tree algebra A = KQ/<R> of finite global dimension, let Ω_A be the finite set of indecomposable A-modules, equivalently the permissible arcs in the modified surface model. For S ⊆ Ω_A, let cl_A(S) be the set of indecomposable summands lying in the resolving subcategory generated by S together with the projective modules. The conjecture is that cl_A is a convex-geometry closure operator: in particular, it satisfies anti-exchange. Explicitly, if C is resolving-closed, x and y are distinct indecomposables not in C, and x ∈ cl_A(C ∪ {y}), then y ∉ cl_A(C ∪ {x}). This is finite, falsifiable by computation on gentle trees, and would imply that the poset of resolving subcategories of a gentle tree algebra is meet-distributive.
domain_bridges: resolving subcategories as finite closure systems
indecomposable string modules as arcs in a surface model
tilting modules as maximal compatible arc configurations
anti-exchange closure operators and convex geometries
proof_strategy: Formalize the modified surface model for a gentle tree algebra as finite combinatorial data: arcs, projective arcs, and the forcing rules generated by extensions and kernels of epimorphisms. Prove that the resolving closure computed by these local forcing rules is a closure operator. Then prove anti-exchange by induction on the number of vertices of the underlying tree, removing a leaf and checking the finitely many local configurations involving the adjacent relation. The key combinatorial lemma should show that if adding an arc y forces a new arc x over a closed set C, then the unique minimal chain of local forcings from y to x is oriented by the tree order and cannot be reversed without already forcing y from C.
title: Anti-exchange for resolving closure in gentle tree algebras

description: For any dimension n ≥ 2, among all n-dimensional orthogonal flat tori of unit volume, the equilateral torus (with all lattice side lengths equal) uniquely maximizes the zeta regularized determinant of the Laplacian. Formally, if T_l = ℝⁿ/(l₁ℤ × ⋯ × lₙℤ) with ∏lᵢ = 1 and lᵢ > 0, then det_ζ(Δ_{T_l}) ≤ det_ζ(Δ_{T_eq}) with equality if and only if l₁ = ⋯ = lₙ = 1, where T_eq is the equilateral torus. This validates Sarnak's conjecture in the orthogonal setting.
proof_strategy: Express the zeta regularized determinant on an orthogonal torus in terms of Epstein-type zeta functions of the lattice. Show log-concavity of the determinant as a function of the logarithmic side-length parameters using the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality and convexity properties of the Epstein zeta function. The unique maximizer follows from strict concavity of the log-determinant functional on the simplex of unit-volume configurations.
title: The Equilateral Torus Uniquely Maximizes the Zeta Regularized Determinant Among Orthogonal Flat Tori of Unit Volume

description: Let $A(z)$ be the ordinary generating series of Pólya trees, with coefficients $a_n$, and let $\rho$ be its radius of convergence such that $A(\rho) = 1$. Then for all integers $k \ge 1$ and all real numbers $t$ such that $0 \le t < \rho$, the truncation error of the $k$-th partial sum is bounded by $0 \le A(t) - \sum_{i=1}^k a_i t^i \le \frac{(t/\rho)^{k+1}}{1 - t/\rho}$.
proof_strategy: Define the Pólya tree generating function $A(z)$ and its radius of convergence $\rho$. Establish the bound $a_k \le \rho^{-k}$ from the fact that $A(\rho) = 1$. Use this coefficient bound to dominate the tail of the series by a geometric series, yielding $\sum_{i \ge k+1} a_i t^i \le \sum_{i \ge k+1} (t/\rho)^i = \frac{(t/\rho)^{k+1}}{1 - t/\rho}$.
title: Pólya Tree Generating Series Taylor Approximation Error Bound

description: Conjecture: Let r,t,n be natural numbers with 1 ≤ t ≤ r and n ≥ r+1. Let K be a pure r-dimensional simplicial complex on n vertices which is r-down path connected. Suppose that for every face σ of K with |σ| = r - t, the reduced homology group H_t(lk_K(σ); ℝ) vanishes. Then q_{r-1}(K) = t n - (t-1)(r+1) if and only if K is isomorphic to Δ_{r+1-t} ⋆ Δ_{n-r-1+t}^{t}. Equivalently, the large lower bound on n appearing in the paper’s equality characterization is unnecessary.
domain_bridges: local link homology constraints ↔ extremal spectral radius
pure simplicial complexes ↔ uniform hypergraphs with downward closure
r-down path connectivity ↔ irreducibility of the signless up-Laplacian
join of a simplex with a skeleton ↔ extremal Perron-equality structure
proof_strategy: Formalize the paper’s inequality proof via the Rayleigh quotient for the nonnegative signless up-Laplacian. Use r-down path connectivity to obtain irreducibility and hence a strictly positive Perron vector. Analyze every equality condition in the chain of inequalities: local homology vanishing should force the relevant link shadows to attain their extremal Kruskal-Katona-type lower bounds, while equality in the Perron/Rayleigh estimates should force all maximal r-faces to contain a common core of size r+1-t and to contain every t-subset of the complementary vertex set. The remaining task is to replace the paper’s large-n rigidity lemma by an exact finite rigidity lemma for the equality case.
title: Threshold-free equality case for the local-homology signless Laplacian bound

description: For any left-regular bipartite graph G of degree d ≥ 3 with girth at least 2s (equivalently, G is s-optimal), the binary linear code B(G) has minimum distance at least 2(d-1)^{s-2}. This conjecture asserts that the girth characterization of s-optimal expanders proven in the paper transfers to a strong lower bound on the minimum distance of the associated code, providing the coding-theoretic foundation needed for the post-quantum key exchange application.
proof_strategy: Use the girth ≥ 2s condition to show that any nonempty subset X ⊆ L with |X| < 2(d-1)^{s-2} cannot have all right vertices with even-degree neighborhoods (the parity condition defining B(G)), by arguing that the local tree structure around small sets forces at least one right vertex to have odd degree in the induced subgraph. The factor of 2 arises from the bipartite structure and the even-girth constraint.
title: Girth-Implied Minimum Distance Bound for Optimal Small-Set Expander Codes

description: The paper demonstrates that augmenting the 27-vertex unit-distance graph G27 with a specific pair of vertices results in a 29-vertex graph with geometric fractional chromatic number strictly greater than 4. The authors note that such augmentations are exceedingly rare. This conjecture posits that, up to Euclidean isometry, this specific 2-vertex augmentation is the unique way to add two vertices to G27 such that the resulting unit-distance graph has a geometric fractional chromatic number strictly greater than 4.
proof_strategy: Formalize the 27-vertex graph G27 and the convex polytope of its 23 extremal geometric fractional colorings. Then, perform a verified exhaustive search or algebraic classification over all possible 2-vertex additions, verifying that only the specific pair identified in the paper yields a unit-distance graph where the geometric fractional chromatic number exceeds 4.
title: Uniqueness of the Critical 2-Vertex Augmentation of G27

description: For integers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 2k+2, any τ_k-maximal graph G of order n has exactly (k+1)(n-1)-1 edges. This resolves the conjecture proposed in the paper by upgrading the established upper bound to an exact equality.
proof_strategy: Assume for contradiction that G is a τ_k-maximal graph with fewer than (k+1)(n-1)-1 edges. Using the Nash-Williams/Tutte characterization, analyze the properties of the partitions of V(G) that violate the condition for k+1 edge-disjoint spanning trees, and show that adding any edge in the complement cannot create a subgraph admitting k+1 edge-disjoint spanning trees, contradicting τ_k-maximality.
title: Exact Edge Count of τ_k-maximal Graphs

description: For any odd prime p and non-negative integer w, the number of 2-balanced p-regular partitions with p-core κ and p-weight w is independent of κ and equals C(w + (p−3)/2, w), where a partition λ is 2-balanced p-regular if it is p-regular and every hook of λ whose length is divisible by p has even arm length. This is the key enumeration result from the paper, connecting the crystal-reflection invariance of d-balanced partitions to an explicit binomial counting formula via RoCK blocks.
proof_strategy: First formalize partitions, Young diagrams, hook lengths, arm/leg lengths, p-regular partitions, p-cores, and p-weights. Then prove that crystal (affine) reflections preserve the 2-balanced property, establishing that the count is independent of the p-core. This reduces the problem to counting 2-balanced p-regular partitions in RoCK blocks, where explicit combinatorial analysis yields the binomial formula C(w + (p−3)/2, w). The core-weight decomposition and RoCK block machinery constitute the major formalization bottleneck.
title: Enumeration of 2-balanced p-regular partitions by p-weight

description: The 29-vertex unit-distance graph G_29, obtained by augmenting the 27-vertex configuration G_27 of Matolcsi et al. with two specific vertices, has geometric fractional chromatic number strictly greater than 4. This is the core technical result of the paper, from which the main theorem (existence of a unit-distance graph with independence ratio below 1/4) and the corollary that the fractional chromatic number of the plane exceeds 4 both follow via the blow-up framework.
proof_strategy: Formalize the 27-vertex configuration G_27 as an explicit point set in R^2 with its unit-distance graph structure. Define geometric fractional chromatic number as the optimum of a linear program over Borel measurable vertex-weighting functions. Characterize the 23 extremal geometric fractional colorings of G_27 as vertices of an 11-dimensional polytope (the key computational step). Show that for the specific two-vertex augmentation, every optimal coloring of G_27 forces a constraint violation on the new vertices, implying the LP optimum must strictly exceed 4. The polytope characterization reduces the verification to checking constraints at finitely many extremal points.
title: Geometric fractional chromatic number of the 29-vertex augmented configuration exceeds 4

description: For the prime $k=7$ (which corresponds to $s=2k+4=18$), the only integer solutions to the Diophantine equation $P_{18}(n) = t^p$ for any prime $p \ge 11$ are the trivial ones $(n,t) = (0,0)$ and $(1,1)$. This formalizes the authors' expectation that there are no additional solutions beyond those explicitly found for smaller primes, an assertion they state is implied by GRH and the weak effective abc conjecture.
proof_strategy: Adopt the authors' proposed conditional approach by assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (to rule out solutions for $11 \le p \le 31$) and the weak effective abc conjecture with $r=1.63$ (to rule out solutions for $p > 31$), or unconditionally extend the linear forms in logarithms and modular methods to computationally verify the remaining prime exponents.
title: No Non-Trivial Higher Prime Powers in 18-gonal Numbers

description: For any integer n ≥ 3, the minimum number of elements in a poset whose automorphism group is isomorphic to Z_2 × Z_{2^n} is 2^{n+1} + 2.
proof_strategy: Formalize the definition of β(G) as the infimum (or minimum) cardinality of a poset P such that Aut(P) ≅ G. Establish the upper bound by constructing a specific poset of size 2^{n+1} + 2 with the required automorphism group. Establish the lower bound by analyzing the orbit structure, minimal elements, and automorphism constraints of any poset realizing Z_2 × Z_{2^n}, demonstrating it must contain at least 2^{n+1} + 2 elements.
title: Minimum Size of a Poset Realizing Z_2 x Z_{2^n}

description: The Diophantine equation $14n^2 - 13n = t^3$ has exactly five integer solutions: $(0, 0)$, $(1, 1)$, $(13, 13)$, $(-1, 3)$, and $(-8, 10)$. This corresponds to the exceptional case $k=13$ in Theorem 1(ii) of the paper, where $P_{30}(n) = t^3$ has the additional solutions $(-1,3)$ and $(-8,10)$ alongside the trivial ones.
proof_strategy: Translate the Diophantine equation $14n^2 - 13n = t^3$ into an elliptic curve by substituting variables to obtain a Weierstrass form. Compute the Mordell-Weil group of this elliptic curve over the rationals, determining its rank and generators. Map the rational points back to integer solutions $(n,t)$ and verify that exactly these five solutions exist.
title: Finiteness of Integer Solutions to the Cubic Triacontagonal Number Equation

description: For any odd prime p and any non-negative integer w, the number of 2-balanced p-regular partitions with p-core κ and p-weight w is independent of the p-core κ and equals C(w + (p-3)/2, w). A partition λ is 2-balanced and p-regular if it is p-regular (no part repeated p or more times) and every hook of λ whose hook length is divisible by p has even arm length.
proof_strategy: First formalize partitions, hook lengths, arm lengths, p-regular partitions, p-cores, p-weight, and 2-balanced partitions. Prove the key structural lemma that crystal (affine) reflection operators preserve 2-balancedness, which implies the count depends only on p-weight w and not on the p-core. Then establish the bijection with RoCK blocks and compute the count via the explicit binomial formula, verifying it matches C(w + (p-3)/2, w).
title: Count of 2-balanced p-regular partitions in a block of p-weight w

description: For positive integers M and non-negative integers n, define f_{M,n}(t) as (-1)^n times the coefficient of u^n in the formal power series expansion of (u;t)_M / (-u;t)_M, where (u;t)_M = ∏_{i=0}^{M-1}(1 - u*t^i). The paper establishes that f_{M,n}(t) is a polynomial in t with non-negative integer coefficients and a palindromic coefficient sequence. We conjecture that f_{M,n}(t) is unimodal for all M ≥ 1 and n ≥ 0, meaning its coefficient sequence weakly increases then weakly decreases.
proof_strategy: Express f_{M,n}(t) using the paper's Gaussian-binomial formula as a sum of products of Gaussian binomial coefficients with t-power weights. Then apply O'Hara's theorem on unimodality of Gaussian binomial coefficients, combined with closure properties of unimodal sequences under convolution and products, to establish unimodality of f_{M,n}(t).
title: Unimodality of Modified GJZ Mixed Scalar Factor Coefficients

description: Characterize the set of limit points of the largest matching roots $\mu(G)$ for all finite graphs $G$. Specifically, prove that the set of limit points contains the interval $[\tau^{1/2} + \tau^{-1/2}, \infty)$ and identify the discrete structure of limit points below the threshold $\tau^{1/2} + \tau^{-1/2}$, where $\tau$ is the golden ratio.
proof_strategy: The strategy involves formalizing the matching polynomial as a coefficient-based polynomial and using the property that for trees, the matching root coincides with the spectral radius. One would use the theory of Perron-Frobenius eigenvalues for graph adjacency matrices and extend it to the matching polynomial using the fact that the matching polynomial of any graph $G$ divides the characteristic polynomial of its path-tree (Godsil's theorem). The proof would require constructing graph sequences via graph operations (like adding vertices or edges) that converge to specific real numbers, utilizing the continuity of the largest root with respect to graph limits.
title: Limit Points of Largest Matching Roots of Graphs

description: Conjecture that for any two linear recurrence sequences derived from a generalized Ankeny–Brauer–Chowla polynomial and its reciprocal with distinct degree parameters, there are at most two common terms exceeding a computable bound depending on the polynomial coefficients.
proof_strategy: Apply Baker's theory of linear forms in logarithms to bound heights of common terms, then use function field and Galois-theoretic constraints to limit the number of large coincidences.
title: Large common values of generalized Ankeny-Brauer-Chowla recurrences

description: The 27-vertex unit-distance graph G_27 constructed by Matolcsi, Ruzsa, Varga, and Zsámboki has geometric fractional chromatic number exactly 4. Adding two suitably chosen augmentation vertices (at specific positions in the plane) yields a 29-vertex unit-distance graph whose geometric fractional chromatic number is strictly greater than 4. This is the key technical step that, combined with the blow-up framework of Matolcsi et al., implies the existence of a finite unit-distance graph with independence ratio below 1/4 and that the fractional chromatic number of the plane exceeds 4.
proof_strategy: First formalize the geometric fractional chromatic number for finite point configurations in the plane. Then characterize all 23 extremal optimal geometric fractional colorings of G_27 (which form a polytope of affine dimension 11). Finally, verify that for every convex combination of these 23 extremal colorings, the two augmentation vertices cannot both be properly colored, forcing the geometric fractional chromatic number above 4. The verification reduces to checking finitely many linear constraints over the extremal colorings.
title: The 29-vertex augmented unit-distance graph has geometric fractional chromatic number strictly greater than 4

description: For every prime power q ≥ 2, the expected coverage time of the coupon collector process under uniform sampling from the line set of the projective plane PG(2,q) strictly exceeds the expected coverage time under uniform sampling from all (q+1)-subsets of a (q²+q+1)-element set. The paper establishes this for q=2 (the Fano plane) and verifies it computationally for small q, but a general proof remains open.
proof_strategy: Compare the two expected coverage times via their inclusion-exclusion representations. The key structural difference is that any two lines of PG(2,q) intersect in exactly one point, creating negative correlations that slow coverage, whereas random (q+1)-subsets have binomially-distributed intersection sizes. One might attempt to show that the Fano/Fano-like intersection structure maximizes the second-order inclusion-exclusion terms, or develop a coupling argument showing the projective plane mechanism is stochastically dominated in coverage by the full model.
title: Projective Plane Mechanisms Dominate Full Model in Coupon Collection

description: Every pairwise reflection-symmetric Latin square (a generalized Latin rectangle with λ=1) of order n is isotopic to the Cayley table of an elementary abelian 2-group. This formalizes the authors' conjecture that the group-theoretic structure observed in computational searches is unavoidable for the base case of λ=1, explaining why existence requires n to be a power of two.
proof_strategy: Normalize the PRS Latin square such that the first row and column are in natural order. Show that the pairwise reflection-symmetry condition implies that the binary operation defined by the normalized Latin square is both commutative and satisfies the exponent-2 property (x ∘ x = e), thus defining an elementary abelian 2-group.
title: Pairwise Reflection-Symmetric Latin Squares are Elementary Abelian 2-Groups

description: The conjecture asserts that for irreducible admissible generic representations π₁ and π₂ of GL₆(F) with identical central characters, the local γ-factor of the exterior cube representation twisted by a sufficiently ramified character χ remains stable, leveraging geometric realizations via the E₆ maximal parabolic subgroup and invariants of the quotient U_M\N'.
proof_strategy: Asymptotic expansion of partial Bessel integrals and vanishing of highly ramified Mellin transforms, combined with structure theory for generic representations.
title: Stability of Exterior Cube γ-Factors under Central Character Equality

description: This conjecture examines the existence of finite unit-distance graphs in the plane with independence ratio below 1/4, offering a falsifiable direction for constructive geometric graph theory.
proof_strategy: Constructive refinement of the geometric fractional chromatic number sequence
title: Proving that unit-distance graphs with low independence ratios exist

catalog_references: Nash-Williams-Tutte theorem on spanning tree packing
description: Every τ_k-maximal graph on n vertices (with n ≥ 2k+2) has exactly (k+1)(n-1)-1 edges. A graph is τ_k-maximal if it contains no subgraph with k+1 edge-disjoint spanning trees, yet adding any edge from its complement creates such a subgraph.
proof_strategy: Use the Nash-Williams/Tutte criterion to show that any τ_k-maximal graph must achieve the upper bound. Assume for contradiction that |E(G)| < (k+1)(n-1)-1, then construct an edge e in Gᶜ such that G+e still lacks k+1 edge-disjoint spanning trees, violating τ_k-maximality.
title: Edge count equality for τ_k-maximal graphs

description: We conjecture that for any deformation parameters t and s the mixed product of the modified Greaves‑Jing‑Zhu operators yields a scalar factor that can be expressed as a rational function of infinite q‑Pochhammer symbols: F(t,s;u) = (u;t)_\u221e (‑u;s)_\u221e / ((‑u;t)_\u221e (u;s)_\u221e). Moreover, the q‑expansion of F(t,s;u) has palindromic coefficients and satisfies a finite‑order linear recurrence; after removing the alternating signs the coefficients are non‑negative integers.
proof_strategy: The conjecture can be approached by first expressing the mixed product via the diagonal conjugation that relates the modified operator to the classical neutral operator. Using known product formulas for neutral operators and Bailey‑pair theory, one can reduce the mixed product to a ratio of infinite q‑Pochhammer symbols as stated. The resulting rational function is then analyzed via standard q‑series techniques (e.g., the pentagonal number theorem) to extract its q‑expansion, prove palindromicity and derive a finite‑order recurrence. The non‑negativity of the sign‑adjusted coefficients follows from known positivity results for principal specializations of one‑row Schur Q‑functions and can be formalized using Lean’s algebraic number theory libraries.
title: Generalized scalar factor for mixed modified Greaves‑Jing‑Zhu operators

description: Conjecture: The set of limit points of the largest matching roots of all finite simple graphs is exactly L = { 2 * cos(π/k) | k ∈ ℕ, k ≥ 3 } ∪ [ √τ + τ^{-1/2}, ∞ ), where τ = (1+√5)/2 is the golden ratio. In particular, for each integer k ≥ 3 there exists a sequence of pairwise distinct graphs (G_n) such that μ(G_n) → 2 * cos(π/k) as n → ∞.
proof_strategy: To show that each 2*cos(π/k) is a limit point, construct a family of graphs consisting of a path P_{m_k} (whose largest matching root equals 2*cos(π/(m_k+1))) together with a bounded‑size gadget whose largest matching root is strictly less than 2*cos(π/k). By choosing m_k → ∞ so that 2*cos(π/(m_k+1)) ↑ 2*cos(π/k) and taking disjoint unions with the gadget, the largest matching root of the union equals that of the path and converges to 2*cos(π/k). Distinctness is ensured by varying m_k. The converse direction (no other limit points below √τ+τ^{-1/2}) follows from known bounds on matching roots of graphs with maximum degree ≤ 2 and a discharging argument that any graph with larger degree forces its largest matching root to exceed the threshold, combined with the characterization of limit points via rooted trees.
title: Limit points of largest matching roots below the golden‑ratio threshold

Miller's original conjecture for symmetric groups
description: Conjecture that the error term in the asymptotic count of entries not divisible by ℓ in the character table of GL₂(𝔽_q) is O(q³) rather than O(q³+ε).
domain_bridges: connections between character divisibility and equidistribution
analytic number theory techniques in representation theory
proof_strategy: Refine existing equidistribution arguments to extract sharper bounds on character vanishing behavior
title: Refined Asymptotic for Non-Divisible Entries in GL₂(𝔽_q) Character Tables

description: The triangle map, a multi-dimensional continued fraction algorithm, possesses a natural extension that can be partitioned into four subdomains. This conjecture posits that the transformation representing the natural extension is equivariant under a discrete symmetry group acting on these subdomains, which is a dynamical analogue of the Young conjugation symmetry found in integer partitions.
proof_strategy: The proof would require constructing the explicit invariant measure for the natural extension of the triangle map in $d$ dimensions. One must then define a transformation $S$ on the domain of the natural extension (the space of $d$-dimensional vectors) and show that $S$ commutes with the map $T$ (the triangle map) and corresponds to the combinatorial operation of Young conjugation when applied to the partition-theoretic interpretation of the map's-digits.
title: Symmetry of the Natural Extension of the Triangle Map via Young Conjugation

description: For any sequence of growing preferential attachment graphs with degree exponent τ ∈ (2,3) whose local weak limit is a continuous-time branching process with power-law offspring distribution of exponent τ, the bond percolation critical window and component size scalings are identical to those of the inhomogeneous random graph with preferential attachment kernel. Specifically, the critical retention probability satisfies p_c(n) = Θ(n^((τ-3)/(2τ-2))), and the largest component size L₁(p_n) exhibits three regimes: (1) p_n ≫ p_c(n) ⇒ L₁(p_n) = Θ_P(n p_n^((τ-1)/(3-τ))) with uniqueness; (2) n^(1/(1-τ)) ≪ p_n ≪ p_c(n) ⇒ L₁(p_n) = Θ_P(n^(1/(τ-1)) p_n) with non-uniqueness; (3) p_n = Θ(p_c(n)) ⇒ L₁(p_n)/√n converges in distribution to a non-degenerate limit characterized by a subcritical Norros-Reittu graph.
proof_strategy: Establish local weak convergence of the preferential attachment graph sequence to a continuous-time branching process with power-law offspring. Develop a coupling between bond percolation on the finite graphs and a percolated branching process. Use the objective method to transfer the critical window analysis from the solvable inhomogeneous random graph model to the general class, leveraging the universality of the scaling limits of the associated exploration processes.
title: Universality of critical percolation scaling for preferential attachment graphs with infinite variance

description: For the affine quiver of type Ã_n with any acyclic orientation, the source-sink pair is the unique banded pair whose coordinate projection fails to fill its band. Specifically, for any pair of vertices (v, w) with δ_v = δ_w (which holds for all pairs in Ã_n since all null-root coefficients equal 1), the projection π_{vw}(C(Q)) fills its band if and only if {v, w} is not the source-sink pair of the given orientation. This extends the paper's complete resolution for the source-sink orientation to all acyclic orientations.
proof_strategy: Extend the AR defect obstruction from the source-sink orientation to arbitrary acyclic orientations. The paper identifies the Auslander-Reiten defect as the sole obstruction to band-filling, and shows it is detected as a coordinate difference c_v - c_w exactly for the source-sink pair in the source-sink orientation. For a general acyclic orientation, the source and sink vertices of the resulting directed path still form a distinguished pair. One must show: (1) the AR defect of the regular component is always detected as the coordinate difference for the source-sink pair regardless of orientation, (2) it is never detected for any other banded pair, and (3) the filling characterization via AR defect applies uniformly across all orientations. The topological interpretation via signed crossing number against the core curve of the annulus may provide an orientation-independent argument.
title: Source-sink uniqueness of non-filling banded pairs in affine type Ã

description: For the parametric harmonic zeta function ζ_H(s,a,b) = Σ_{n≥0} H_n(a)/(n+b)^s where H_n(a) = Σ_{k=1}^n 1/(k+a) is the generalized harmonic number and ψ denotes the digamma function, the Laurent expansion at the double pole s=1 satisfies: (1) the leading coefficient of (s-1)^{-2} equals 1, independent of both a and b; (2) the coefficient of (s-1)^{-1} equals -ψ(a+1), independent of b. This generalizes the known pole structure of the classical harmonic zeta function ζ_H(s) = ζ_H(s,0,1) and formalizes the residue computation announced in the paper for the parametric case.
proof_strategy: Decompose H_n(a) = ψ(n+a+1) - ψ(a+1) via the digamma function to write ζ_H(s,a,b) = Σ_{n≥0} ψ(n+a+1)/(n+b)^s - ψ(a+1)·ζ(s,b). The first sum inherits its leading singularity from the asymptotic ψ(n+a+1) ~ log(n) as n→∞, contributing (s-1)^{-2} to the pole at s=1 (analogous to how -ζ'(s) contributes (s-1)^{-2}). The second term -ψ(a+1)·ζ(s,b) contributes -ψ(a+1)·(s-1)^{-1} from the simple pole of the Hurwitz zeta. Careful estimation of the digamma-weighted Dirichlet series using Mellin transform techniques confirms that subleading corrections from b and from the 1/(2n) term in the digamma asymptotic do not alter these leading two Laurent coefficients.
title: Laurent expansion coefficients of the parametric harmonic zeta function at its double pole s=1

description: Every optimal 1-planar graph with connectivity 6 is (5,5)-linked. Formally, for any 6-connected optimal 1-planar graph G and any two disjoint vertex subsets S1, S2 of size 5, there exist vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs G1, G2 of G such that S1 is contained in the vertex set of G1 and S2 is contained in the vertex set of G2.
proof_strategy: First formalize optimal 1-planar graphs (1-planar graphs with exactly 4|V| - 8 edges) and graph connectivity. Then establish structural properties of 6-connected optimal 1-planar graphs, likely leveraging their tight connection to triangulations. Use these structural properties and high edge density to show that any two disjoint 5-element vertex subsets can be covered by disjoint connected subgraphs, proving the (5,5)-linked property.
title: 6-Connected Optimal 1-Planar Graphs are (5,5)-Linked

catalog_references: Neumaier's classification of strongly regular graphs
description: The conjecture posits that non-trivial first homology groups arise only in specific exceptional cases like the Petersen graph or similar structures under Neumaier's classification, ruling out triviality in other contexts.
domain_bridges: Linking to finite field properties and graph theory over specified families
proof_strategy: Formalizing consequences of Neumaier's conditions using algebraic constructs in Lean
title: Trivial Homology Exceptions

description: For all integers $k \ge 1$, $n \ge 0$, and $s \in \mathbb{Z}$, the coefficient of $q^n z^s$ in the normalized Jacobi triple product tail $J_k(z,q)$ is a non-negative integer. This resolves Merca's stronger nonnegativity conjecture on truncated Jacobi triple product series and generalizes the coefficientwise positivity of truncated pentagonal number series.
proof_strategy: Define the formal bivariate series $J_k(z,q)$ and the generalized minimal-excludant for partitions. Construct the sign-reversing involution to show that the coefficients of $J_k(z,q)$ correspond to alternating sums of sizes of invariant subsets. Then formalize the injective lift operator on Frobenius arms combined with Konan's size- and length-preserving bijection to prove the invariant subsets are weakly increasing in $k$, which directly implies the non-negativity of the coefficients.
title: Coefficientwise Positivity of Normalized Jacobi Triple Product Tails

description: Conjecture that for any integers d>1, e>1 with (e-3) divisible by d, the number of d-balanced e-regular partitions in a block of e-weight w equals the binomial coefficient \(\binom{w + (e-3)/d}{w}\).
domain_bridges: Representation theory of the symmetric group
proof_strategy: Show that crystal (affine) reflections preserve the d-balanced property, then use RoCK block structure to establish a recurrence on w whose unique solution is the binomial coefficient, and formalize this induction in Lean.
title: Binomial Count Conjecture for d-balanced e-regular Partitions

description: Conjecture that a Latin square of order n is pairwise reflection‑symmetric (i.e., for every pair of columns each ordered symbol pair (p,q) occurs as often as its reversal (q,p)) if and only if n is a power of two. This captures the claimed λ=1 case and is falsifiable by exhibiting a counterexample for a non‑power‑of‑two n or proving impossibility.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit pairwise reflection‑symmetric Latin squares for n = 2^k using affine permutations of the vector space (GF(2))^k, and prove non‑existence for other n by parity or orbit‑counting arguments.
title: Pairwise Reflection-Symmetric Latin Squares Exist Exactly for Powers of Two

description: This paper proposes a computational framework to determine homology groups of simplicial complexes through discrete Morse theory and gradient vector fields, offering a formalizable path for practical applications.
proof_strategy: Constructive existence argument via combinatorial dimension tracking
title: A combinatorial approach to the effective nerve theorem

description: For any regular n-maniplex M, the automorphism group of its flag graph, the automorphism group of its 1-skeleton graph, and the automorphism group of its 1-coskeleton graph are all isomorphic to each other and to the automorphism group of M itself. This conjecture formalizes the claim that different canonical graph representations of regular maniplexes preserve their symmetry structure.
proof_strategy: Show that the natural projection maps from the flag graph to both the 1-skeleton and 1-coskeleton graphs are covering maps that induce isomorphisms on automorphism groups for regular maniplexes, leveraging the fixed-point-free involution structure and vertex-transitivity properties established in the paper.
title: Automorphism Group Equivalence for Regular Maniplex Graph Representations

catalog_references: Sign law for Ramanujan's third order mock theta function ρ(q)
description: Let ρ(q) = ∑_{n≥0} r(n) q^n be Ramanujan's third order mock theta function defined by ρ(q) = ∑_{m≥0} q^{2m(m+1)} / ∏_{k=1}^{m} (1 + q^{2k-1} + q^{4k-2}). Then r(3n) > 0 for all n ≥ 0; r(3n+1) ≤ 0 and r(3n+2) ≤ 0 for all n ≥ 0, with the only zeros being r(2) = r(4) = r(8) = r(11) = r(20) = 0.
proof_strategy: Use Watson's identity 2ρ(q) + ω(q) = T(q) to relate ρ(q) to the mock theta function ω(q) and a theta-eta product T(q). Obtain explicit Rademacher-type expansions with rigorous error bounds for the coefficients of ω(q) and T(q). Combine these to derive explicit inequalities for r(n) for all sufficiently large n, and verify the remaining small n by direct computation.
title: Finite sign conjecture for Ramanujan's third order mock theta function ρ(q)

description: The paper proves that every spherical (weight 0) automorphic form on SL(2,Z)\H decomposes into a cusp form and a linear combination of Laurent coefficients of the standard Eisenstein series, using only Green's identity and basic analysis. We conjecture that the same direct proof strategy extends to automorphic forms of any integer weight k, yielding a decomposition of the space A_k(X) into cusp forms of weight k and the span of Laurent coefficients of the weight k Eisenstein series.
proof_strategy: Extend the automorphic Green's identity to weight k Eisenstein series and automorphic forms. Use the meromorphic continuation and functional equation of the weight k Eisenstein series. Show that the boundary terms in the Green's identity for the truncated weight k Eisenstein series yield the projection onto the cuspidal subspace and the Laurent coefficients at the poles.
title: Generalization of Franke's theorem to higher weight automorphic forms via Green's identity

description: Let K be the function field of a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a p-adic field. For any smooth, proper, geometrically integral, rationally connected K-variety X, the unramified cohomological obstruction with respect to H^3_nr(X, Q/Z(2)) coincides with the descent obstruction: X(A_K)^{H^3_nr} = X(A_K)^{descent}. This is the analogue over p-adic function fields of Colliot-Thélène's conjecture that the Brauer-Manin obstruction is the only obstruction for rationally connected varieties over number fields, replacing the Brauer-Manin obstruction with the unramified obstruction as justified by cohomological dimension constraints.
proof_strategy: Follow the strategy of the number field case: (1) establish that the unramified obstruction is contained in the descent obstruction (already shown in the paper for general smooth integral varieties), (2) prove the reverse inclusion by showing that any descent obstruction arising from a torsor under a commutative linear algebraic group can be detected by H^3_nr(X, Q/Z(2)), using the arithmetic dualities and Poitou-Tate-style exact sequences developed for p-adic function fields, (3) for rationally connected varieties, leverage the vanishing of higher unramified cohomology beyond degree 3 to show the descent obstruction cannot be strictly finer.
title: Unramified Obstruction Equals Descent Obstruction for Rationally Connected Varieties over p-adic Function Fields

description: For every integer n ≥ 4, there exists a diagonal quantum Latin square of order n (DQLS(n)) with maximum cardinality n², meaning all n² entries are pairwise distinct up to a global phase, and both the main diagonal and anti-diagonal each form an orthonormal basis of the n-dimensional Hilbert space.
proof_strategy: Establish base cases n = 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 via direct constructions using row-quantum Latin rectangles and special complete mappings of finite groups, then apply the singular direct product construction recursively to extend existence to all n ≥ 4, leveraging the algebraic properties of complete mappings in groups of odd order and direct products for even orders.
title: Existence of Maximum Cardinality Diagonal Quantum Latin Squares for All Orders n ≥ 4

description: For every ε > 0, there exists T₀(ε) > 0 such that for all T ≥ T₀(ε), ∫₀ᵀ |ζ(1/2 + it)|⁶ dt ≥ (42 - ε) · c₃ · T · (log T)⁹, where c₃ = a₃/9! and a₃ is the Keating–Snaith arithmetic factor defined by the Euler product ∏_p (1 - 1/p)⁹ Σ_{m≥0} (Γ(m+3)/(Γ(m+1)·Γ(3)))² · p⁻ᵐ. This asserts that the lim inf of M₃(T)/(c₃·T·(log T)⁹) equals 42, matching the Keating–Snaith conjecture from the lower bound side, and would improve the current unconditional constant of 34.1 established in the paper.
proof_strategy: Extend the two-piece amplification method of the paper by optimizing the amplifier weights over a wider class of Dirichlet polynomials, potentially incorporating shifted-convolution estimates and spectral theory of automorphic forms. The current method achieves 34.1 out of the conjectured 42; closing the gap requires either stronger amplification or a hybrid approach combining amplification with the resonator method of Radziwiłł–Soundararajan, plus refined estimates for the off-diagonal main terms that currently are only captured partially.
title: Sharp lower bound for the sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function

description: For any partition λ of n and any support pattern S ⊆ [n] × [n], the number of n × n nilpotent matrices over F_q with Jordan canonical form type λ and support contained in S is a polynomial in q with non-negative integer coefficients. This extends known polynomiality results for Hessenberg supports (connected to chromatic quasisymmetric function evaluations via Shareshian–Wachs theory) and directly addresses the polynomiality questions the paper raises for more general support patterns and prescribed affine slices of adjoint orbits.
domain_bridges: Algebraic geometry (Hessenberg varieties and Springer fibers)
Representation theory (Hall-Littlewood polynomials and Green functions)
Combinatorics (chromatic quasisymmetric functions and rook theory)
proof_strategy: Leverage the paper's Hall scalar product formula expressing the count in terms of skew modified Hall-Littlewood functions and q-Whittaker functions. For Hessenberg supports, connect to chromatic quasisymmetric functions and the Shareshian-Wachs theorem relating Hessenberg variety point counts to chromatic quasisymmetric function evaluations. For general supports, develop combinatorial-algebraic tools showing the relevant Hall scalar products specialize to polynomials in q, potentially using geometric methods on Springer fibers and deformation arguments to reduce arbitrary supports to Hessenberg-type patterns.
title: Polynomiality of Nilpotent Matrix Counts with Prescribed Support

description: There exists a finite unit-distance graph G in the Euclidean plane whose independence ratio α(G)/|V(G)| is strictly less than 1/4. This answers Erdős's 1987 question in the negative and implies that the fractional chromatic number of the plane χ_f(ℝ²) > 4. The proof relies on showing that a two-vertex augmentation of the 27-vertex configuration G₂₇ from Matolcsi et al. yields a point configuration with geometric fractional chromatic number strictly greater than 4.
proof_strategy: Formalize the 27-vertex graph G₂₇ as an explicit point configuration in ℝ², characterize its 23 extremal geometric fractional colorings as a polytope of affine dimension 11, then show that adding two suitably chosen vertices yields a configuration where every fractional coloring assigning weight ≤ 1/4 per color class fails to cover all vertices, establishing χ_gf > 4. The blow-up steps from Matolcsi et al. then translate this into a finite unit-distance graph with α(G)/|V(G)| < 1/4.
title: Existence of a finite unit-distance graph in the plane with independence ratio strictly less than 1/4

description: The Diophantine equation $P_{14}(n) = t^4$ has exactly five solutions in integers $(n,t)$: $(0,0)$, $(1,1)$, $(1,-1)$, $(-2000, 70)$, and $(-2000, -70)$. This corresponds to the specific case $k=5$ (where $s=2k+4=14$) in Theorem 1(i) of the paper, which fully lists the solutions for this sub-family.
proof_strategy: Reduce the equation $6n^2 - 5n = t^4$ to finding integer points on an elliptic curve via appropriate variable substitutions. Then, apply the Mordell-Weil sieve and/or Chabauty's method to rigorously bound and determine all rational points, finally filtering for the integer solutions and verifying them in Lean.
title: Complete classification of 4th powers in the 14-gonal numbers

description: The paper proves that for integers $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2k+2$, any $\tau_k$-maximal graph on $n$ vertices has at most $(k+1)(n-1)-1$ edges, and constructs examples achieving this bound. The authors conjecture that this upper bound is actually an exact equality: every $\tau_k$-maximal graph on $n \ge 2k+2$ vertices has exactly $(k+1)(n-1)-1$ edges. This conjecture is verified for $k=1$, but remains open for $k \ge 2$.
proof_strategy: Assume for contradiction that there exists a $\tau_k$-maximal graph $G$ with $|E(G)| < (k+1)(n-1)-1$. By the definition of $\tau_k$-maximality, $G$ has no subgraph with $k+1$ edge-disjoint spanning trees, but adding any edge creates one. Use the Nash-Williams/Tutte characterization to analyze the specific partitions of $V(G)$ that restrict the spanning tree packing number. Show that the edge deficiency implies the existence of an edge $e \in E(G^c)$ such that $G+e$ still fails to satisfy the Nash-Williams/Tutte condition for $k+1$ edge-disjoint spanning trees, thereby contradicting the $\tau_k$-maximality of $G$.
title: Exact Edge Count of Tau_k-Maximal Graphs

description: For any positive integer M and non-negative integer k, the principal specialization of the one-row Schur Q-function q_k evaluated at 1, t, ..., t^{M-1} (which equals the coefficient of u^k in the formal power series expansion of ∏_{i=0}^{M-1} (1+ut^i)/(1-ut^i)) is a polynomial in t with non-negative integer coefficients, which is palindromic of degree k(M-1).
proof_strategy: Define P_{M,k}(t) as the coefficient of u^k in the formal power series expansion of the product ∏_{i=0}^{M-1} (1+ut^i)/(1-ut^i) over ℤ[[u]][t]. Prove that the coefficients of P_{M,k}(t) are non-negative integers by induction on k using the recurrence relation for one-row Schur Q-functions. Prove palindromicity by establishing the functional equation t^{k(M-1)} P_{M,k}(1/t) = P_{M,k}(t), which can be derived from the symmetry of the generating function under the substitution u -> u t^{M-1}.
title: Palindromicity and Non-Negativity of Principal Specializations of One-Row Schur Q-Functions

description: The number of 2-balanced p-regular partitions in any block of p-weight w for an odd prime p is precisely the binomial coefficient C(w + (p-3)/2, w). A partition is 2-balanced p-regular if it is p-regular and every hook of length divisible by p has an even arm length.
proof_strategy: Formalize partitions, Young diagrams, hooks, and arm lengths. Define p-regularity and the 2-balanced condition. Establish blocks, p-cores, and p-weights. Prove that the count is independent of the p-core by demonstrating that crystal reflections preserve the 2-balanced property, and finally compute the count explicitly in a RoCK block to arrive at the binomial formula.
title: Enumeration of 2-balanced p-regular partitions in blocks

The angular equidistribution result for n=2 suggests that the arguments of nonzero character values become uniformly distributed, which should similarly force ℓ-divisibility proportions to vanish for all n.

description: A pairwise reflection-symmetric Latin square of order n exists if and only if n is a power of 2. A pairwise reflection-symmetric Latin square is an n×n matrix with entries from {1,...,n} where each row and column is a permutation, and for every pair of distinct columns (j₁,j₂) and every ordered pair of symbols (p,q), the row-index set where (p,q) appears in columns (j₁,j₂) has the same cardinality as the row-index set where (q,p) appears. Since each column is a permutation, this means (p,q) appears in some row if and only if (q,p) also appears in some row. The forward direction (necessity) requires showing no such Latin square exists when n has an odd prime factor, while the backward direction (sufficiency) constructs one from the Cayley table of the elementary abelian 2-group (Z/2Z)^k.
proof_strategy: Sufficiency: Construct the Latin square from the Cayley table of (Z/2Z)^k; since every element is self-inverse, the pairwise column condition (p,q)↔(q,p) holds because p+j₁=q+j₂ iff q+j₁=p+j₂ (as j₁=j₁⁻¹ in exponent-2 groups). Necessity: Show that if n has an odd prime factor, the pairwise reflection-symmetry condition forces a contradiction via parity arguments on the permutation structure relating column pairs—specifically, the column-relabeling permutation between any two columns must be an involutory derangement, and counting constraints from the Latin square structure become incompatible when n is not a power of 2.
