title: β(Z₂ × Z_{2^n}) = 2^{n+1} + 2 for all positive integers n

description: For every prime k with 5 ≤ k ≤ 97 and every prime p ≥ 11, the Diophantine equation (k+1)n² - kn = t^p (equivalently, P_{2k+4}(n) = t^p) has no integer solutions beyond the trivial ones (n,t) = (0,0) and (1,1). This conjecture asserts unconditionally what the paper establishes conditionally under GRH (for 11 ≤ p ≤ 31) and the weak effective abc conjecture with exponent r = 1.63 (for p > 31). The unconditional proof for p = 5, 7 and for p > p_0(2k+4) is already given in the paper; the conjecture closes the remaining gap for intermediate primes p.
proof_strategy: The paper already reduces the problem to ruling out at most one exceptionally large solution per prime exponent p in the range 11 ≤ p ≤ p_0(2k+4), where p_0 is enormous (involving 10^100000). A complete unconditional proof would require either: (1) significantly sharper effective bounds for linear forms in logarithms to eliminate the 'at most one large solution' regime without GRH, or (2) new descent arguments specific to the factored form n((k+1)n - k) = t^p that exploit the structure of the polynomial (k+1)n² - kn for each fixed k. The modular method, already applied in the paper for small p, would need to be extended systematically to all remaining exponents.
title: No non-trivial prime-power solutions in specific polygonal number sequences

description: Every $\tau_k$-maximal graph on $n$ vertices has exactly $(k+1)(n-1)-1$ edges, for integers $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2k+2$. A graph $G$ is $\tau_k$-maximal if it contains no subgraph admitting $k+1$ edge-disjoint spanning trees (i.e., its spanning tree packing number $\tau(G) \le k$), but adding any edge from its complement creates a graph that does admit $k+1$ edge-disjoint spanning trees (i.e., $\tau(G+e) \ge k+1$ for all $e \notin E(G)$).
proof_strategy: The authors have already established the upper bound $|E(G)| \le (k+1)(n-1)-1$. To prove the conjecture, one must establish the matching lower bound $|E(G)| \ge (k+1)(n-1)-1$. This likely involves induction on $k$ and $n$, leveraging the Nash-Williams/Tutte theorem to relate edge counts across partitions, and analyzing the structural properties and edge-connectivity bounds of $\tau_k$-maximal graphs to show that fewer edges would contradict the maximality condition.
title: Exact Edge Count of $\tau_k$-Maximal Graphs

description: For every positive integer M and integer k with 0 ≤ k ≤ M, define a_{M,k}(t) as the absolute value of the coefficient of u^k in the expansion (u;t)_M / (-u;t)_M = Σ_{k=0}^{M} (-1)^k a_{M,k}(t) u^k, where (u;t)_M = Π_{j=0}^{M-1}(1 - u t^j) and (-u;t)_M = Π_{j=0}^{M-1}(1 + u t^j). The paper establishes that each a_{M,k}(t) is a palindromic polynomial in t with nonnegative integer coefficients (being signed principal specializations of one-row Schur Q-functions). The conjecture is that each a_{M,k}(t) is also unimodal as a polynomial in t: if a_{M,k}(t) = Σ_{i=0}^{d} c_i t^i, then there exists j such that c_0 ≤ c_1 ≤ ··· ≤ c_j ≥ c_{j+1} ≥ ··· ≥ c_d. Since a_{M,k}(t) is palindromic, this is equivalent to the first half of the coefficient sequence being weakly increasing.
proof_strategy: Exploit the identification of a_{M,k}(t) as a principal specialization of a one-row Schur Q-function q_k(1, t, t^2, ..., t^{M-1}) and apply techniques from the theory of unimodal log-concave sequences. Specifically: (1) show that a_{M,k}(t) can be realized as the rank-generating function of a ranked poset that is rank-symmetric and satisfies the Lefschetz property, implying unimodality via the hard Lefschetz theorem for posets; or (2) establish a combinatorial interpretation via lattice paths with restricted steps and apply the theory of log-concave sequences via injections; or (3) express a_{M,k}(t) as a positive sum of Gaussian binomial coefficients and leverage known unimodality results for such coefficients.
title: Unimodality of the Mixed Scalar Factor Coefficients

description: Every real number greater than or equal to τ^(1/2) + τ^(-1/2), where τ = (√5 + 1) / 2 is the golden ratio, is a limit point of the largest matching roots of finite simple graphs. Specifically, for any such real number γ, there exists a sequence of graphs whose largest matching roots are all distinct and converge to γ. This implies that the set of limit points contains the entire interval [τ^(1/2) + τ^(-1/2), ∞).
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit sequence of finite simple graphs (such as paths with attached star graphs or other specific compositions) whose largest matching roots can be continuously tuned to converge to any given real number γ ≥ τ^(1/2) + τ^(-1/2). The proof involves showing that the set of achievable largest matching roots is dense in this interval or directly forms the continuum, likely utilizing the interplay between the matching polynomial and the characteristic polynomial of paths/trees to produce the desired limits.
title: Limit Point Continuum of Largest Matching Roots

description: The set of optimal geometric fractional colorings of the 27-vertex unit-distance graph G₂₇ constructed by Matolcsi, Ruzsa, Varga, and Zsámboki, viewed as a convex polytope in the space of measurable assignments, has exactly 23 extreme points and affine dimension 11. This finite characterization is the key structural fact enabling the two-vertex augmentation that pushes χ_gf strictly above 4, and it can in principle be verified by solving the associated linear program with 182304 variables.
proof_strategy: Formalize G₂₇ as an explicit 27-vertex unit-distance graph with its coordinates. Encode the geometric fractional chromatic number as a linear program over measurable functions. Use the finite-dimensional reduction (the LP with 182304 variables capturing the constraints on finite sub-configurations) to extract the extreme points computationally. Verify each of the 23 extremal colorings satisfies all unit-distance constraints and achieves total weight exactly 4, and confirm no other extreme points exist via vertex enumeration on the LP's feasible polytope.
title: Extremal Geometric Fractional Colorings of G₂₇ Have Exactly 23 Vertices

description: For every prime power q, the fair mechanism given by the line set of the projective plane PG(2,q) over the finite field F_q has strictly greater expected coverage time than the full model (uniform distribution on all (q+1)-subsets of a (q²+q+1)-element set). Specifically, if E_PG(q) denotes the expected time to collect all n = q²+q+1 coupons when each draw uniformly selects a line of PG(2,q), and E_full(q) denotes the expected time under uniform selection from all binom(n, q+1) possible (q+1)-subsets, then E_PG(q) > E_full(q) for all prime powers q.
proof_strategy: Establish the inequality E_PG(q) > E_full(q) by computing or bounding the expected coverage times via inclusion-exclusion. The expected coverage time for a fair mechanism F on [n] with block size ℓ is E[F] = ∫₀^∞ (1 - ∏_{S∈F}(1 - e^{-|S∩T|t}/|F|)) dt for the set T of already-collected coupons, which can be reformulated as E[F] = ∑_{k=1}^{n} (-1)^{k+1} ∑_{A∈([n] choose k)} 1/(1 - P_F(A)) where P_F(A) is the probability a random block from F contains A. The key comparison reduces to showing that the projective plane mechanism has a larger sum over k-subset intersection statistics than the full model. Use the fact that in PG(2,q), every pair of distinct points lies on exactly one line, and every line has exactly q+1 points, to compute the k-wise intersection probabilities exactly and compare term by term with the full model.
title: Projective Plane Mechanisms Dominate the Full Model in Expected Coverage Time

description: For λ = 1, a pairwise reflection-symmetric generalized Latin rectangle is precisely a pairwise reflection-symmetric Latin square of order n, which exists if and only if n is a power of two. This conjecture states that every such Latin square is isotopic to the Cayley table of the elementary abelian 2-group (Z/2Z)^k where n = 2^k, formalizing the paper's hypothesis that an underlying group-theoretic structure is unavoidable in this setting.
proof_strategy: Translate the pairwise reflection symmetry condition into the property that the permutation mapping any column to another in the Latin square is an involution. Use the theory of Latin squares and quasigroups to show that this property forces the corresponding quasigroup to be isotopic to an associative quasigroup of exponent 2, which is necessarily an elementary abelian 2-group.
title: Unavoidable Group-Theoretic Structure in Pairwise Reflection-Symmetric Latin Squares

description: For any integer $t \ge 2$ and $n \ge 28t - 17$, the unique $tK_3$-free graph of order $n$ with maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius is the join graph $K_{t-1} \vee K_{\lfloor(n-t+1)/2\rfloor, \lceil(n-t+1)/2\rceil}$.
proof_strategy: Formalize the signless Laplacian matrix as Q(G) = D(G) + A(G) and its spectral radius as its largest eigenvalue. Define the tK3-free property as the absence of t pairwise vertex-disjoint triangles. Define the graph join operation and complete bipartite graphs. Establish the extremality and uniqueness by translating the asymptotic bounds and perturbation arguments from the paper into exact computations, ultimately showing that any deviation from the specified join structure either violates the tK3-free condition or decreases the spectral radius.
title: Extremal Signless Laplacian Spectral Radius of tK3-Free Graphs

description: For any integer $n \ge 3$, the minimum size of a finite poset realizing $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ as its automorphism group is $2^{n+1} + 2$.
proof_strategy: Define β(G) as the minimal cardinality of a finite poset P such that Aut(P) is isomorphic to G. Establish the upper bound by constructing a specific poset of size 2^{n+1} + 2 with the desired automorphism group, relying on the product with Z2 construction. Establish the lower bound by showing any poset realizing Z2 x Z_{2^n} must have at least 2^{n+1} + 2 elements, analyzing the orbit structure and fixed points of the automorphism group action.
title: Minimum Poset Size for Automorphism Group Z2 x Z2^n

description: For every prime power q ≥ 2, consider the fair mechanism given by uniformly sampling lines of the projective plane PG(2,q), where n = q² + q + 1 is the number of points and ℓ = q + 1 is the line size. The expected coverage time of this projective plane mechanism strictly exceeds that of the full model (uniform sampling of all ℓ-subsets of an n-element set). This generalizes the paper's Fano plane (q=2) counterexample to the Grunbaum–Yaakobi conjecture and posits that projective plane line sets systematically yield slower fair mechanisms than the full model across all orders.
proof_strategy: Express the expected coverage time as E[T] = Σ_{k≥0} (1 - P_k), where P_k is the probability that k independent draws cover all n coupons. For the full model, P_k is computed via inclusion-exclusion over all ℓ-subsets. For PG(2,q), exploit the fact that any two lines meet in exactly one point, which increases overlap between draws relative to the full model where pairwise overlaps are smaller and more variable. Specifically, the probability two random lines share a specific point is 1/(q²+q+1)·1/q in PG(2,q), versus the uniform pairwise overlap in the full model. Use generating functions or the inclusion-exclusion structure to show the projective plane's higher-order intersection pattern yields uniformly lower coverage probabilities P_k at each k, hence a larger sum and strictly greater E[T]. An inductive argument on q, combined with the known closed-form for E[T] under BIBD-type mechanisms, may reduce the inequality to an algebraic statement about the parameters.
title: Projective Plane Coupon Mechanisms Dominate the Full Model

description: For any integers d, e > 1, a partition λ is d-balanced (with respect to e) if every hook of λ whose length is divisible by e has arm length divisible by d. The conjecture states that the affine crystal reflection operators on partitions preserve the d-balanced property: for any d, e > 1, any d-balanced partition λ, and any valid crystal reflection index i, the partition s_i(λ) obtained by applying the i-th affine crystal reflection to λ is again d-balanced.
proof_strategy: Define partitions, hook lengths, arm lengths, and d-balanced property in Lean. Formalize the affine crystal reflection operators on partitions (via abacus configurations or node addition/removal). The key step is showing that if h_{rc}(λ) ≡ 0 (mod e) implies a_{rc}(λ) ≡ 0 (mod d), then the same holds after applying a crystal reflection s_i. This likely proceeds by analyzing how a single affine reflection modifies hook lengths and arm lengths, using the fact that the reflection changes the partition by adding/removing a rim hook of e-residue i, and checking the d-balanced condition is preserved at each affected node.
title: Crystal Reflections Preserve d-Balanced Property of Partitions

description: Every pairwise reflection-symmetric Latin square of order n = 2^k (equivalently, every PRGLR(2^k, 1)) is isotopic to the Cayley table of the elementary abelian 2-group (ℤ/2ℤ)^k. This formalizes the paper's conjecture that 'group-theoretic structure may even be unavoidable' for these objects, specialized to the minimal λ = 1 regime where existence is exactly characterized by n being a power of two.
proof_strategy: Step 1: Show that pairwise reflection symmetry at λ = 1 forces the Latin square to satisfy the quadrangle condition (Belousov's criterion), which implies isotopy to a group Cayley table. Step 2: Exploit the reflection-symmetry constraint to show the group must be abelian: for any columns c₁, c₂, the equal-frequency condition on ordered pairs (p,q) and (q,p) forces commutativity of the underlying operation. Step 3: Show every element must be an involution (g ∘ g = e) since reflection symmetry with identical column pairs forces g = g⁻¹, yielding exponent 2. Step 4: Conclude the group is (ℤ/2ℤ)^k by the classification of finite abelian groups.
title: Elementary Abelian 2-Group Structure is Unavoidable in Pairwise Reflection-Symmetric Latin Squares

description: For all integers $t \ge 2$ and $r \ge 2$, there exists an integer $n_0(t, r)$ such that for all $n \ge n_0(t, r)$, the unique graph of order $n$ achieving the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius among all $tK_{r+1}$-free graphs is $K_{t-1} \vee T_r(n-t+1)$, where $T_r(m)$ is the Turán graph on $m$ vertices with $r$ parts. This extends the paper's Theorem 1.1 from $tK_3$-free graphs to general $tK_{r+1}$-free graphs, mirroring the known results for the adjacency spectral radius.
proof_strategy: Adapt the stability method and spectral techniques used for the adjacency spectral radius by Ni, Wang, and Kang to the signless Laplacian matrix, bounding the spectral radius for graphs close to the extremal structure and showing that any structural deviation reduces the signless Laplacian spectral radius.
title: Signless Laplacian Spectral Turán Conjecture for $tK_{r+1}$-Free Graphs

description: For all sufficiently large positive integers u, the only integer solutions (x, y) to the parametric Thue equation x(x - uy)(x - u²y)(x - u³y) + y⁴ = 1 are the five trivial solutions (1, 0), (0, 1), (u, 1), (u², 1), and (u³, 1). This extends the proved degree-3 case of Thomas's conjecture (where P₁(u) = uᵏ, P₂(u) = uˡ) to degree 4 with Pⱼ(u) = uʲ for j = 1, 2, 3, and connects to the generalized ABC polynomial framework via the associated Thue equation Yᑫ π_U(X/Y) = 1.
proof_strategy: Extend the degree-3 approach by combining Baker's theory of linear forms in logarithms to bound solution size, function field techniques to exploit the parametric monomial structure Pⱼ(u) = uʲ, and Galois-theoretic analysis of the degree-4 generalized ABC polynomial's splitting field. The principal new difficulty is managing the additional root u³ and the resulting larger Galois group, which increases the number of fundamental units in the associated S-unit equation.
title: Thomas Conjecture for Degree-4 Parametric Thue Equations with Monomial Substitutions

description: For any p-adic field F, non-trivial additive character ψ, and two irreducible admissible ψ-generic representations π₁, π₂ of GL₆(F) with the same central character, there exists an integer c such that for any character χ of F^× with conductor ≥ c, the local gamma factors satisfy γ(s, π₁⊗χ, ∧³, ψ) = γ(s, π₂⊗χ, ∧³, ψ).
proof_strategy: Formalize p-adic fields, smooth representations, generic representations, and the Langlands-Shahidi local coefficients. Construct the exterior cube representation of GL_6 and the parabolic subgroup of E_6. Compute the invariant measure of the geometric quotient U_M \ N', relate Shahidi's partial Bessel functions to partial Bessel integrals, and prove the asymptotic expansion of these integrals. Conclude by showing the vanishing of highly ramified Mellin transforms to establish the equality of gamma factors.
title: Stability of the Exterior Cube Local Gamma-Factor for GL(6)

description: Two regular maniplexes of rank n ≥ 3 are isomorphic if and only if their 1-skeleton graphs are isomorphic and their 1-coskeleton graphs are isomorphic. The forward direction is immediate since maniplex isomorphisms induce graph isomorphisms on both the 1-skeleton (vertex-edge graph) and 1-coskeleton (facet-ridge graph). The substantive claim is the converse: for regular maniplexes, the pair of boundary graphs uniquely determines the internal flag structure, because regularity (the automorphism group acts regularly on flags) constrains the rank-1-through-rank-(n-2) incidences to be recoverable from how the boundary graphs interlock. This conjecture is motivated by the database interoperability problem: if true, the 1-skeleton and 1-coskeleton suffice as complete identifying invariants for regular maniplexes, eliminating the need to store full flag graphs for classification.
proof_strategy: The forward direction follows from functoriality of the skeleton and coskeleton constructions. For the reverse direction, the key insight is that regularity forces the automorphism group to act regularly on flags, so Aut(M) is determined by a single flag stabilizer. One should show that the intersection of the automorphism groups of the 1-skeleton and 1-coskeleton (lifted to act on flags through the incidence structure) uniquely determines the involutions r_i on the flag graph. Start with rank 3 (maps), where the 1-skeleton and dual graph determine the embedding via the medial graph construction, then induct on rank. Computational verification on the census of regular 4-maniplexes (connected in the paper) would provide evidence.
title: Skeleton-Coskeleton Determination for Regular Maniplexes

description: Let ρ(q) = Σ_{m≥0} q^{2m(m+1)} / Π_{j=0}^{m} (1+q^{2j+1}+q^{4j+2}) = Σ_{n≥0} r(n)q^n be Ramanujan's third-order mock theta function. Then for all n ≥ 0: r(3n) > 0, r(3n+1) ≤ 0, and r(3n+2) ≤ 0. Moreover, the only zeros in the latter two families occur at n = 2, 4, 8, 11, 20, i.e., r(3n+1) = 0 iff n ∈ {0, 1} (giving n=1,4) and r(3n+2) = 0 iff n ∈ {0, 2, 6} (giving n=2,8,20), with the single exception r(11) = 0.
proof_strategy: The asymptotic sign law is proven via Watson's identity 2ρ(q) + ω(q) = T(q) combined with Rademacher-type expansions for ω(q) and the theta-eta product T(q), yielding r(n) ~ κ_{n mod 3} · (2π)/(12n+8)^{1/4} · I_{1/2}(π√(12n+8)/18) where κ₀ > 0, κ₁ < 0, κ₂ < 0. To prove the exact finite conjecture, one must: (1) make the error term in the Rademacher expansion fully effective with explicit constants, yielding an explicit N₀ such that the sign law holds for all n ≥ N₀; (2) computationally verify all cases n < N₀. The effective bound requires careful tracking of all error terms in the circle method analysis, similar to effective Rademacher bounds for partition ranks.
title: Exact sign law for coefficients of Ramanujan's third-order mock theta function ρ(q)

description: The paper proves that $g$ point counts determine the zeta function of a $g$-dimensional abelian variety over $\mathbb{F}_q$ if $q > Q(g)$, where $Q(g)$ is super-exponential. This conjecture asserts that a quadratic bound on $q$ suffices, similar to Kedlaya's bound for $2g$ counts. Specifically, there exists an absolute constant $C$ such that for any integer $g \ge 1$ and prime power $q > Cg^2$, if $A$ and $B$ are abelian varieties of dimension $g$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with equal point counts $\#A(\mathbb{F}_{q^i}) = \#B(\mathbb{F}_{q^i})$ for all $1 \le i \le g$, then $A$ and $B$ have the same zeta function.
proof_strategy: Refine the inductive error analysis from the paper to show that the power sums of the inverse Frobenius eigenvalues can be controlled with polynomial precision. This could involve bounding the coefficients of the L-polynomial more tightly using the functional equation and Weil conjectures bounds, avoiding the exponential blow-up in the current analysis.
title: Polynomial bound for point counts determining zeta functions of abelian varieties

description: For any commutative ring R and matrix A ∈ R^{n×n}, if A is strongly 1-principled (all diagonal entries are 1 and all cyclic products of length > 1 vanish), then A^m is also strongly 1-principled for any m ≥ 1.
proof_strategy: Induction on m and combinatorial expansion of matrix power entries. A cyclic product of A^m expands into a sum of products of cyclic products of A. Since the total length is > 1, at least one factor in each term is a cyclic product of length > 1, which vanishes, causing the entire sum to vanish.
title: Inheritance of strongly 1-principled property under matrix powers

description: For τ in the upper half-plane, define G(τ) = 2E₂(2τ) - E₂(τ) and let t(τ) be the Hauptmodul on Γ₀(2) with q-expansion t = 256q + 4096q² + …. Then the identity E₄(τ)/G(τ)² = (t(τ) + 256)/(t(τ) + 64) holds as an identity of modular functions on Γ₀(2). This is a key technical lemma used to prove that G(τ) satisfies the pulled-back hypergeometric ODE, thereby identifying G with ₃F₂(1/4, 1/2, 3/4; 1, 1; X(τ)).
proof_strategy: Both sides are modular functions on Γ₀(2) (i.e., weight-0 meromorphic modular forms). Clear denominators to obtain a modular form D₁ = (t+64)E₄ - (t+256)G² of weight 4 on Γ₀(2). By the finite divisor check lemma, D₁ is holomorphic and has no poles, so it suffices to verify that its q-expansion vanishes to sufficiently high order. Since the space M₄(Γ₀(2)) is finite-dimensional (dimension 2), checking finitely many q-expansion coefficients forces D₁ = 0. In Lean, one can compute q-expansions as formal power series over ℚ and verify the identity coefficient-by-coefficient up to the Sturm bound.
title: Rational modular ratio for E₄ on Γ₀(2)

description: The paper investigates whether the sequence of graphs representing finite projective planes over finite fields converges log-converges toward a specific random graph model.
proof_strategy: Construct a lemmatic refinement of the lemma governing the limit ratio under logarithmic transformation.
title: Logarithmic convergence of finite projective-plane incidence graphs

description: For any lacunary sequence $(a_n)_{n \geq 1} \subset \mathbb{N}$ satisfying $a_{n+1} \geq q a_n$ for some $q > 1$, and for Lebesgue-almost every $x \in \mathbb{T}$, the maximal circular gap satisfies $\lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{N \cdot G_N(x)}{\log N} = 1$. The paper proves this when $a_n \mid a_{n+1}$ for all $n$, and establishes $\frac{1}{2} \leq \liminf \leq \limsup \leq \frac{q+1}{q-1}$ in general. The conjecture asserts that the divisibility assumption is unnecessary—the limit always exists and equals 1, matching the random i.i.d. model.
proof_strategy: The paper's divisibility proof leverages a martingale structure from the $a_n | a_{n+1}$ condition. For general lacunary sequences, one could attempt: (1) Show the $\Gamma$ parameter defined in the paper satisfies $\limsup N G_N(x)/\log N \leq 1 + \Gamma$ a.e., then prove $\Gamma$ can be made arbitrarily small by passing to subsequences; (2) Approximate a general lacunary sequence by one satisfying divisibility (e.g., replacing $a_n$ with $\prod_{k=1}^n a_k$) and control the gap distortion; (3) Prove the liminf and limsup bounds converge by developing a variance estimate showing $\text{Var}(N G_N(x)/\log N) \to 0$ a.e., using the independence properties of lacunary trigonometric sums.
title: Universal Gap Asymptotic for Lacunary Dilations

description: For every finite group $G$ and integer $d \ge 3$, there exists a $d$-regular graph $\Gamma$ with $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma) \cong G$ that admits both an $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)$-invariant proper $d$-edge-coloring and a strong embedding $\beta$ into an orientable surface such that $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma) \cong \operatorname{Aut}(\beta(\Gamma)) \cong G$.
proof_strategy: Start with the paper's corrected Sabidussi construction, which yields a $d$-regular graph with an invariant proper $d$-edge-coloring. Then, adapt the paper's unbounded genus sequence construction—which replaces edges with specific 2-cell embedded graphs—to also preserve or lift the invariant edge-coloring, ensuring the modified graph simultaneously admits a strong embedding with the prescribed automorphism group and the invariant coloring.
title: Simultaneous Invariant Strong Embedding and Edge-Coloring Realization

description: Every discrete d-pseudomanifold (for d ≥ 1) on a finite vertex set has at least 2(d+1) vertices, as established in the paper. This provides a foundational combinatorial bound for these manifold-like graph structures.
proof_strategy: Define discrete d-pseudomanifolds inductively on d: for d=1, it is an n-cycle (n ≥ 4); for d>1, the induced subgraph on the neighborhood of every vertex must be a discrete (d-1)-pseudomanifold. Prove the vertex bound by induction on d, utilizing the base case of cycles and the fact that the neighborhood condition enforces a minimum degree and structural constraints that bound the total number of vertices from below.
title: Minimum Vertex Bound for Discrete Pseudomanifolds

description: For every even dimension n ≥ 2, every 0 < α < 1/2, and every non-degenerate quadratic form Q on F_q^n (q an odd prime power), there exist constants C_α > 0 and q_α such that for all q ≥ q_α and all E ⊆ F_q^n with |E| ≥ C_α · q^{n/2+1/3}, the distance set Δ_Q(E) = {Q(x−y) : x,y ∈ E} satisfies |Δ_Q(E)| > 1 + α(q−1). This improves the previous threshold exponent (n+1)/2 to n/2+1/3, achieved via a Delsarte linear programming bound on the association scheme of level sets of Q, with eigenvalue estimates relying on Gauss sums and Kloosterman sums via the Weil bound.
proof_strategy: 1) Formalize the association scheme arising from the level sets of a non-degenerate quadratic form Q on F_q^n (even n), establishing the Q-polynomial property and computing the eigenvalues via Gauss sums. 2) Prove the key eigenvalue bound |P_i(0)| ≤ q^{n/4} √(2/(q−1)) using the Weil bound on Kloosterman sums. 3) Construct a feasible solution to the Delsarte linear program yielding the exponent n/2+1/3. 4) Apply the Delsarte LP bound to derive |Δ_Q(E)| > 1+α(q−1) when |E| ≥ C_α q^{n/2+1/3}.
title: Erdős-Falconer Distance Set Threshold n/2+1/3 in Even Dimensions over Finite Fields

description: For all integers n >= 5, the log-convexity gap of Bell numbers is bounded below by a Fibonacci-weighted sum of squares of smaller Bell numbers: B_{n+1} B_{n-1} >= sum_{i=0}^n F_i (B_{n-i})^2, where F_i is the i-th Fibonacci number with F_0 = F_1 = 1.
proof_strategy: Formalize the combinatorial injection mapping pairs of partitions of [n] with the same base to partitions of [n+1], apply the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on the sums grouped by base, and bound the remaining terms recursively using the Fibonacci sequence properties.
title: Fibonacci-Weighted Log-Convexity of Bell Numbers

description: For f a normalized Hecke eigenform for SL(2,Z) (holomorphic of weight k ≥ 2 or Hecke-Maass) with Hecke eigenvalues λ_f(n), and for any ε > 0 with 1 ≤ Y ≤ X^{1/2-ε}, the triple correlation sum satisfies |∑_{n≤X} ∑_{m≤Y} λ_f(n)λ_f(m)λ_f(n+m)| ≪_{f,ε} X^{1/2+ε}Y. This is the optimal bound predicted by Sato-Tate heuristics and random matrix theory, going beyond the non-trivial power-saving bounds established in the paper for bilinear sums of GL(2) Fourier coefficients.
proof_strategy: Apply the delta method of Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec to decouple the constraint n+m, then deploy Voronoi summation in both n and m variables. Use Cauchy-Schwarz to reduce to a shifted convolution sum and apply the Kuznetsov trace formula to express triple products of Fourier coefficients as central L-values via Watson's formula. The crux is obtaining subconvexity for the triple product L-function L(s, f⊗f⊗f) at s=1/2, which GRH supplies but which remains unconditionally open; any unconditional proof would constitute a breakthrough in subconvexity theory.
title: Square-Root Cancellation for GL(2) Triple Correlation Sums

description: The graph algebra $\mathcal{A}_n$ on $n$ vertices, defined as the quotient of the multivariate polynomial ring $K[x_{ij} \mid 1 \le i < j \le n]$ by the ideal $\langle x_{ij}^2 - x_{ij} \rangle$, carries a natural $\mathfrak{sl}_2(K)$-module structure. The action is defined on the monomial basis $x^G$ (where $G$ is a simple graph on $n$ vertices) by $h \cdot x^G = (2|G| - m) x^G$, $e \cdot x^G = \sum_{e' \notin G} x^{G \cup e'}$, and $f \cdot x^G = \sum_{e' \in G} x^{G \setminus e'}$, where $m = \binom{n}{2}$. The conjecture states that as an $\mathfrak{sl}_2(K)$-module, $\mathcal{A}_n$ is isomorphic to the $m$-th tensor power of the standard two-dimensional $\mathfrak{sl}_2(K)$-module $V$.
proof_strategy: First, formalize the graph algebra $\mathcal{A}_n$ as the quotient of the multivariate polynomial ring by the ideal $\langle x_{ij}^2 - x_{ij} \rangle$. Define the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action on $\mathcal{A}_n$ using the explicit formulas for $h$, $e$, and $f$ on the monomial basis $x^G$. Verify the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutation relations $[h,e]=2e$, $[h,f]=-2f$, and $[e,f]=h$ to establish a valid representation. Then, construct a linear map from the $m$-th tensor power of the standard $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module $V^{\otimes m}$ to $\mathcal{A}_n$ by sending basis elements to monomials, and prove it is an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-module isomorphism by showing it preserves the action of the Lie algebra generators and is bijective.
title: Graph Algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-Module Isomorphism to Tensor Power

catalog_references: Masser's relation module theorem for algebraic groups
description: Let E = (G_a^d, φ) be a d-dimensional Anderson t-module defined over a global function field L with constant field F_q, and let P_1, ..., P_ℓ ∈ E(L) be points with logarithmic heights at most H. The F_q[t]-module of relations R = {(a_1, ..., a_ℓ) ∈ F_q[t]^ℓ : Σ a_i · P_i = 0} is finitely generated and free (since F_q[t] is a PID). Conjecture: there exist effective constants C_1, C_2 depending only on q, d, and the t-module E, such that R is generated by elements whose entries have degree at most C_1 · H^{C_2 · ℓ}. This is the function-field analogue of Masser's effective bound on generators of relation modules for points on commutative algebraic groups over number fields, and would provide effective termination bounds for the algorithm presented in the paper.
domain_bridges: Geometry of numbers over function fields (F_q[t]-lattices)
Effective results in Diophantine approximation (Baker's method analogues)
proof_strategy: Via the paper's correspondence, reduce to bounding degrees of polynomial solutions to Frobenius difference equations v^(1) = A·v. Apply the geometry of numbers over the valuation ring F_q[[1/θ]] combined with the theory of rigid analytic t-motives: (1) embed the relation module into a lattice in a rigid analytic space, (2) use successive minima estimates for F_q[t]-lattices analogous to Masser's geometry-of-numbers argument, (3) control the growth of entries under iteration of the Frobenius-twisted equation via height bounds on the t-module action, yielding polynomial degree bounds on generators.
title: Effective Degree Bound for t-Module Relation Modules

description: A conjecture asserting that any triangulation of n vertices guarantees an H-packing of minimal size floor(n/5), forming a tight lower bound.
proof_strategy: direct application of inductive bounds on triangulations
title: Floor(n/5) H-Bounding

description: If P(x)∈ℤ[x] is a self‑reciprocal polynomial of even degree 2m with all roots on the unit circle and leading coefficient not equal to ±1, then at least one root has an argument that is an irrational multiple of τ.
proof_strategy: Search for a counterexample by enumerating small integer self‑reciprocal polynomials with small leading coefficients and checking the rationality of root arguments; a counterexample would falsify the conjecture.
title: Conjecture on irrational angles of non‑monic unit palindromes

description: For almost all even integers N > 0, there exist primes p₁, p₂ with p₁ + p₂ = N and |p₁ - p₂| + 1 having at most 2 prime factors counted with multiplicity (i.e., |p₁ - p₂| + 1 ∈ P₂). This strengthens the paper's P₄ result and would follow from a level of distribution of at least 1/3 for Goldbach primes, compared to the 1/6 level established here.
proof_strategy: Improve the level of distribution of Goldbach primes from θ = 1/6 to θ = 1/3 by refining the Type II exponential sum estimates in the circle method decomposition. The bottleneck is the bilinear sum bound where the well-factorability condition currently limits the level to 1/6. Achieving θ = 1/3 would then permit a Chen-type weighted sieve or Selberg sieve argument to reduce the almost-prime condition from P₄ to P₂ for the difference |p₁ - p₂| + 1, analogous to how Matomäki's well-factorable level 1/2 yields P₂ results under additional hypotheses.
title: Goldbach partitions with semiprime difference

description: For any connected split reductive group G over Q_p, if K and L are anabelomorphic p-adic fields (i.e., Gal_K ≅ Gal_L as topological groups), then the Fargues–Scholze stacks of L-parameters for (G, K) and (G, L) are isomorphic as algebraic stacks. This is Theorem 2.2.1 of the paper, whose formalization would require building the theory of L-parameter stacks and establishing their functorial dependence on the absolute Galois group.
proof_strategy: First formalize the notion of anabelomorphic p-adic fields (topologically isomorphic absolute Galois groups). Then construct the Fargues–Scholze stack of L-parameters as a functor from the category of split reductive groups and topological Galois groups to algebraic stacks. Show this functor factors through the topological isomorphism class of the Galois group, yielding the desired isomorphism of parameter stacks. The split torus case (Theorem 4.1) provides the base case for an inductive argument on the reductive group structure.
title: Anabelomorphic Invariance of Fargues–Scholze Parameter Stacks

description: We propose that the absolute value of random homomorphism values at the root of infinite, locally finite trees with leaves fixed at zero exhibits subgaussian tail bounds governed by effective resistance, extending results from regular trees to all transient trees via comparison with discrete Gaussian-like distributions.
domain_bridges: Electrical network theory (via effective resistance computations)
Stochastic processes on groups (for coarse classification theory)
proof_strategy: Prove a novel large deviation principle for homomorphism models using effective resistance and compare to discrete Gaussian processes via coupling arguments, leveraging recent advances in coarse classification theory for infinite trees.
title: Effective Resistance-Determined Subgaussian Tail Bounds for Random Homomorphisms on Infinite Trees

catalog_references: Zuev's chamber interpretation of threshold functions
Fukuda-Tamura-Tokuyama theorem on average facet counts
description: The paper proves that for a Boolean threshold function f on n variables, if the symmetric-variable extension f^sym on n+1 variables is also threshold, then minimum specification number is preserved (i.e., simplicial chambers map to simplicial chambers). The natural generalization is that the specification number always increments by exactly one under this extension: σ_{n+1}(f^sym) = σ_n(f) + 1. Equivalently, the gap σ_n(f) - (n+1) from the minimum is invariant under symmetric extension whenever the extension is threshold. This would follow from a facet-counting argument showing the chamber for f^sym has exactly one more facet than the chamber for f, via the chamber-facet correspondence established in the paper.
domain_bridges: Hyperplane arrangement chambers ↔ Boolean threshold functions
Simplicial cones ↔ Minimum specification number functions
proof_strategy: Using the chamber-facet correspondence: the chamber C(f) ⊂ A for function f has exactly σ_n(f) facets (corresponding to essential examples). Under symmetric extension, the parameter space gains one dimension and the chamber C(f^sym) is the product of C(f) with a half-line (by the product-with-half-line structure established for other extension operations). This product operation adds exactly one facet (the 'new' facet from the half-line boundary), yielding σ_{n+1}(f^sym) = σ_n(f) + 1. The key step is verifying the symmetric extension induces this product structure on chambers whenever it yields a threshold function.
title: Specification Number Increments by One Under Symmetric Variable Extension

description: An irreducible polynomial P(x) ∈ ℤ[x] of even degree 2d ≥ 4 equals the full reciprocal-radius polynomial P_Γ of some finite connected K_{2d+1}-free graph Γ if and only if P is a Salem polynomial and the coefficient a₁ of x^{2d-1} in P satisfies a₁ ≤ -5. The necessity direction (the first-coefficient obstruction) is established in the paper; the sufficiency direction — that every Salem polynomial meeting this coefficient bound is realizable as some P_Γ — remains open and would yield a complete algebraic-combinatorial characterization of strongly primitive Salem growth rates.
proof_strategy: The necessity direction follows from the independence-polynomial obstruction and the sharp first-coefficient bound a₁ ≤ -5 proven in the paper. For sufficiency, one would need to construct explicit graph families realizing each admissible Salem polynomial. Promising approaches include: (1) inductive constructions using suspension and graph products that preserve the Salem property while adjusting coefficients, (2) analyzing how concatenation operations on defining graphs transform P_Γ to systematically target prescribed coefficient sequences, and (3) classifying minimal obstruction graphs to identify the boundary between realizable and unrealizable Salem polynomials.
title: Salem Clique Polynomial Characterization

catalog_references: chromatic number of the rational plane
description: There exists an absolute constant ε > 0 such that for all sufficiently large n, one can find n rational points in Q^2 determining at least n^{1+ε} unit distance pairs. This conjecture is motivated by algorithmic evidence that rational-plane constructions achieve higher edge density in unit distance graphs than the n^{1+o(1)} density obtainable from integer grid constructions, leveraging the richer Pythagorean structure of Q^2 to surpass grid-based lower bounds for the Erdős unit distance problem.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit families of rational points by exploiting the parametrization of primitive Pythagorean triples (m²-n², 2mn, m²+n²) and their scaled variants to create overlapping unit-distance configurations. The key mechanism: rational points on distinct unit circles can simultaneously realize many unit distances through shared Pythagorean structures. Use the multiplicative density of Gaussian integer norms (r₂(n) ~ divisor function) to show that rescaled Pythagorean configurations create superlinear edge intersections. The algorithmic local-breadth search in Q^2 naturally discovers these overlapping structures that grid-based approaches miss.
title: Superlinear density of unit distance graphs in the rational plane

catalog_references: Chain Covers in the Boolean Lattice
description: For any fixed integer $t \ge 2$, the minimum number of maximal chains $N(n, n-t)$ required to cover all strict $(n-t)$-chains in the Boolean lattice $B_n$ is asymptotically $n!/t$. This generalizes the exact result for $t=2$ and the asymptotic result for $t=3$ established in the paper, conjecturing that the general upper bound of $n!/t$ derived from inversion numbers modulo $t$ is asymptotically tight for all $t$.
proof_strategy: The upper bound $N(n, n-t) \le n!/t$ is already established by partitioning permutations based on their inversion number modulo $t$. The matching lower bound requires generalizing the subcube-hitting and vertex-Turán arguments used for $t=3$ to arbitrary fixed $t$, demonstrating that any family of maximal chains covering all $(n-t)$-chains must have cardinality at least $(1/t - o(1))n!$.
title: Asymptotic Density of Maximal Chain Covers for Near-Maximal Strict Chains

description: For any geometrically irreducible, non-special algebraic curve V in the affine plane A^2 defined over Q with deg(X|_V) ≠ deg(Y|_V), the Weil heights of special points (pairs of CM j-invariants) on V are bounded linearly in the height of V. Specifically, there exist effectively computable constants c₁ depending only on max{deg X, deg Y} such that for every special point (x,y) ∈ V, max{h(x), h(y)} ≤ c₁ + 26·max{deg X, deg Y}³·h(V). This improves upon prior effective results by Kühne and Bilu-Masser-Zannier which had worse (non-linear) dependence on h(V).
domain_bridges: Complex multiplication theory → Height theory (CM points have controlled heights)
Algebraic curve degree theory → Arakelov height of varieties
proof_strategy: The proof proceeds by: (1) establishing that when deg X ≠ deg Y, the curve V satisfies a 'weakly bounded height' condition—meaning the height of V controls the heights of the coordinate functions in a linear fashion; (2) using the theory of complex multiplication to bound the heights of CM j-invariants in terms of their discriminants; (3) applying the Pila-Wilkie counting theorem to the o-minimal structure generated by the j-function and its derivatives to bound the number and size of rational points on definable sets associated to V; (4) combining these to derive the linear dependence on h(V), contrasting with the polynomial dependence in earlier approaches that could not exploit the degree inequality.
title: Effective André's Theorem with Linear Height Dependence for Curves with Unequal Coordinate Degrees

description: For a finite extension K/Q_p, a monic polynomial f ∈ O_K[X] of degree ≥ 2 satisfying f'(X) ∈ m_K·O_K[X] (equivalently f̄ ∈ k[X^p]), and a compatible inverse branch (t_n) with t_0 ∈ O_K and f(t_{n+1}) = t_n, define K_n = K(t_n), E_n = K_n ∩ K^{ur}, and e_n = [K_n : E_n]. If e_n > 1 for some n, then e_n → ∞ as n → ∞. This is the key intermediate result in the proof of the paper's main theorem (Theorem 1.2), establishing that iterated polynomial towers under the purely inseparable reduction condition exhibit a ramification dichotomy: either the tower is entirely unramified over the maximal unramified subextension, or the ramification indices grow without bound.
proof_strategy: Construct the tower K_n inductively. The condition f̄ ∈ k[X^p] ensures the reduction of f factors through Frobenius. When ramification first appears at level n₀ (i.e., e_{n₀} > 1), apply a uniform valuation estimate: since f'(X) ∈ m_K·O_K[X], the Taylor expansion gives v_K(f(t_{n+1}) - f(s)) ≥ v_K(t_{n+1} - s) + 1 for suitable s, forcing successive roots to have strictly growing valuation discrepancies. This recursive lower bound on v_K(t_{n+1} - t_n) propagates through the tower, showing that each ramified step compounds the ramification index over the maximal unramified subfield. The reduction step (subtracting unramified residue lifts) ensures we may assume positive-valuation conditions at the ramified tail, after which the uniform estimate forces e_n to be unbounded.
title: Unbounded Ramification Indices in Iterated p-Adic Polynomial Towers

description: Every mod 2 toric-colorable PL (n-1)-sphere with n ≤ 5 admits a Z-characteristic map. Equivalently, for PL spheres of dimension at most 4, mod 2 toric-colorability implies Z-toric-colorability. This generalizes the paper's computational verification that all 198,846 mod 2 toric-colorable seeds of dimension 4 and Picard number 5 are toric-colorable to all such spheres of dimension ≤ 4, regardless of Picard number. The conjecture asserts that the only obstruction to lifting a Z_2-characteristic map to a Z-characteristic map vanishes for PL spheres of dimension ≤ 4.
proof_strategy: Use the binary matroid framework to parametrize all mod 2 characteristic maps on low-dimensional PL spheres. Develop an obstruction theory for lifting Z/2Z-characteristic maps to Z-characteristic maps, identifying the obstruction in terms of cohomology classes. Show that the relevant cohomological obstructions (related to orientability and compatibility conditions on the sphere) vanish for PL spheres of dimension ≤ 4, using the classification of low-dimensional PL spheres and structural properties of the contraction categories from the paper's dynamic programming framework.
title: Mod 2 to Z Characteristic Map Lifting for Low-Dimensional PL Spheres

description: For some absolute constant C, any subset A of {1, ..., N} with cardinality at least 5N/8 + C contains distinct elements a, b, c such that a+b, a+c, and b+c are all in A. This resolves Erdős Problem 865 and corresponds to Theorem 1.1 of the paper.
proof_strategy: Induction on the size of the set, utilizing the folded additive lemma (Lemma 2.1) and the centering argument, mirroring the paper's reduction from a coarse bound to the sharp bound.
title: Sharp 5/8 Bound for Erdős-Sós Pairwise-Sums Problem

description: Let $f_1, \dots, f_k \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be distinct irreducible polynomials with positive leading coefficients, and let $S_f$ be the set of integers $a$ such that $f_i(a)$ is prime for all $i$. Let $\overline{S_f}$ be the closure of $S_f$ in the profinite completion of $\mathbb{Z}$, and let $\nu$ be the procounting measure on $\hat{\mathbb{Z}}$. The profinite Bateman-Horn conjecture proposes that the procounting measure of $\overline{S_f}$ is equal to the Bateman-Horn Euler product constant $C(f)$.
proof_strategy: Formalize the procounting measure on the profinite integers, define the Bateman-Horn Euler product constant $C(f)$, and establish that the measure of the closure of the prime-generating set equals $C(f)$. This bridges the topological properties of $\hat{\mathbb{Z}}$ with the analytic properties of the Euler product, starting with the base case $f(x)=x$ where $C(f)=1$.
title: Profinite Bateman-Horn Conjecture for Polynomials over Z

description: For a Steinhaus random multiplicative function f, the ratio E[|∑_{x≤n≤x+y} f(n)|²] / y converges to 1 if and only if y = o(x / (log x)^{log 4 - 1}). This precisely identifies the phase transition where the natural normalization √y ceases to yield a standard Gaussian limit, connecting to the exponent log 4 − 1 ≈ 0.386 that appeared in Soundararajan–Xu's earlier range and which the current paper overcomes by introducing a corrected normalization.
proof_strategy: Compute the second moment E[|∑_{x≤n≤x+y} f(n)|²] exactly as a sum over pairs (m,n) in [x,x+y]² sharing prime factors, decompose by the size of gcd(m,n), and analyze the dominant contribution from coprime pairs (giving y) versus correlated pairs (contributing a correction term of order y·(log x)^{1−log 4} when y is near the threshold). Show the correction is o(y) iff y = o(x/(log x)^{log 4 − 1}).
title: Phase transition for variance asymptotics of Steinhaus short-interval sums

description: For any graph G with maximum degree d, there exists a signing σ of its edges such that the spectral radius of the signed adjacency matrix A_σ is at most 2√(3(d-1)).
proof_strategy: Formalize the method of interlacing polynomials and mixed characteristic polynomials for the sum of independent random rank-1 matrices. Establish the upper bound on the largest root of the mixed characteristic polynomial to derive the spectral bound for the signed adjacency matrix.
title: Improved Bilu-Linial Spectral Bound via Interlacing Families

description: The 27-vertex unit-distance graph G₂₇ constructed by Matolcsi, Ruzsa, Varga, and Zsámboki has geometric fractional chromatic number exactly 4. There exists a two-vertex augmentation G₂₉ of G₂₇ (obtained by adding two suitably chosen points to the point configuration) that is still realizable as a unit-distance graph in ℝ² and has geometric fractional chromatic number strictly greater than 4. Concretely: there exist points p₂₈, p₂₉ ∈ ℝ² such that the graph G₂₉ on 29 vertices, with edges determined by unit distance among all 29 points, satisfies χ_gf(G₂₉) > 4.
proof_strategy: Define G₂₇ as an explicit 27-point configuration in ℝ² with coordinates. Define the geometric fractional chromatic number χ_gf(G) as the optimum of a linear program over measurable colorings invariant under the Euclidean motion group. First establish χ_gf(G₂₇) = 4 by characterizing all 23 extremal geometric fractional colorings (forming a polytope of affine dimension 11). Then identify two augmentation points p₂₈, p₂₉ such that every optimal coloring of G₂₇ forces a unit-distance conflict with at least one of p₂₈ or p₂₉, which by LP duality pushes the objective value strictly above 4. The blow-up steps of Matolcsi et al. then propagate this to independence ratio < 1/4.
title: Strictly super-4 geometric fractional chromatic number of the augmented Matolcsi–Ruzsa–Varga–Zsámboki graph

description: Every real number greater than or equal to √(√5 + 2) is a limit point of the set of largest matching roots of simple graphs. Specifically, for any real number γ ≥ √(√5 + 2), there exists an infinite sequence of simple graphs whose largest matching roots are all distinct and converge to γ.
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit family of graphs (e.g., using paths with pendant edges or specific tree families) parameterized such that their largest matching roots continuously approach any given γ ≥ √(√5 + 2). Utilize the interlacing properties of matching polynomials and the intermediate value theorem on the continuous dependence of roots on graph parameters to establish convergence and distinctness.
title: Density of Largest Matching Root Limit Points Above Golden Ratio Threshold

description: For any odd prime p, let G = (Z/p^2 Z)^2 and H = pG. Then the transversal difference number δ(G,H) = (2p-1)^2. This conjecture identifies the first genuinely new residual obstruction beyond cyclic quotients and product families with one nonsplit cyclic coordinate.
proof_strategy: The paper reduces the problem to analyzing transversals as graphs of functions F_p^2 → F_p^2 with carry-corrected finite-field derivative images. A proof would likely require extending this derivative analysis, potentially using algebraic-geometric properties of the polynomial maps arising from the transversal condition, or establishing tight bounds on the union of derivative image fibers via combinatorial methods over F_p.
title: Transversal Difference Number for the Same-Prime Square Plane

description: Every triangle-free graph on $N$ vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $N^2/25$ edges. Equivalently, for any triangle-free graph $G$ on $N$ vertices, the bipartization number $\beta(G) \le N^2/25$. The bound is tight, achieved by the balanced blow-up $C_5[N/5]$.
proof_strategy: Extend the per-root-MaxCut envelope and blow-up integrality techniques to arbitrarily large N, resolve the medium-density band using higher-order flag algebra certificates verified in exact rational arithmetic, and provide stability analysis to transition to the extremal C_5[N/5] configuration.
title: Erdős n²/25 Max-Cut Conjecture

description: For each dimension d ≥ 1, the Young conjugation involution σ_Y on the natural extension (Ω_d, T̃_d, μ_d) of the d-dimensional triangle map—induced by transposition of Young diagrams (swapping parts and multiplicities in the integer partition interpretation)—is a μ_d-measure-preserving involution that conjugates T̃_d to its inverse: σ_Y ∘ T̃_d ∘ σ_Y = T̃_d^{-1} holds μ_d-almost everywhere. This time-reversal property explains the four-fold decomposition of Ω_d into subdomains of equal invariant measure documented in the source paper: the Klein four-group generated by σ_Y and the involution induced by the matrix transpose symmetry of the triangle map partition matrices yields four fundamental domains Ω_d^(σ) for σ ∈ {id, σ_Y, σ_T, σ_Y∘σ_T}, each of measure μ_d(Ω_d)/4. The result is non-trivial even for d = 1 (Farey/Gauss map case).

For d = 1, verify explicitly using the known natural extension of th
title: Young Conjugation is a Time-Reversal Symmetry of Triangle Map Natural Extensions

description: For the inhomogeneous random graph with preferential attachment kernel κ_{β,γ}(x,y) = β(x ∧ y)^{-γ}(x ∨ y)^{γ-1} where γ ∈ (1/2, 1) (equivalently, degree exponent τ = 1 + 1/γ ∈ (2,3)), the rescaled ordered component sizes in the critical percolation window converge to a multiplicative coalescent. Specifically, parametrizing p_n(t) = β · n^{(τ-3)/(2τ-2)} · (1 + t · n^{-(3-τ)/(2(τ-1))}) for t ∈ ℝ, the process (n^{-1/2} · C_{(k)}(G_n(p_n(t))))_{k ≥ 1, t ∈ ℝ} converges in distribution in the Skorokhod topology on ℓ²↓ × ℝ to a multiplicative coalescent with merger rate κ_{β,γ}(x_i, x_j) between components carrying marks x_i, x_j, where the initial mark distribution is the Norros–Reittu intensity of the associated subcritical graph. This extends Aldous' multiplicative coalescent limit for Erdős–Rényi graphs and the Bhamidi–van der Hofstad–Hooghiemstra dynamic scaling results for finite-variance inhomogeneous random graphs to the infinite-variance preferential attachment setting, and provides a process-level refinement of the static convergence in distribution established in the paper.
proof_strategy: 1) Establish a dynamic coupling between percolation processes at different retention probabilities to show the component merging dynamics are well-approximated by multiplicative coalescent transitions with the preferential attachment kernel. 2) Characterize the limiting mark distribution using the Norros-Reittu representation of the subcritical graph, verifying it belongs to the appropriate ℓ²↓ initial condition class. 3) Prove the susceptibility function χ(p, n) diverges with the predicted exponent at the critical point, providing the necessary entrance boundary condition for the coalescent. 4) Generalize the Aldous–Limic abstract convergence criterion for multiplicative coalescents to accommodate inhomogeneous kernels with power-law mark distributions (infinite variance). 5) Verify the tightness of the rescaled component size processes in ℓ²↓ using the star-shaped component structure identified in the subcritical regime.
title: Multiplicative Coalescent Scaling Limit for Critical Percolation on Preferential Attachment Graphs with Infinite Variance Degrees

description: For every dimension d ≥ 2 and every heat time T > 0, the infinite-volume large-N limit of normalized Wilson loop expectations in heat-kernel Yang-Mills theory on Z^d with structure group U(N) and N-scaled heat time T/N per plaquette exists. Precisely: for every loop γ on Z^d, the limit Φ_T(γ) := lim_{N→∞} lim_{V→Z^d} (1/N) E_{V,N,T}[Tr(W_γ)] exists, where the inner limit is over exhausting sequences of finite sublattices V ⊂ Z^d. This extends the paper's strong-coupling existence result (which requires T > T₀(d) for a dimension-dependent threshold) to the entire positive real line, establishing the master field across all coupling regimes. For d = 2 this should follow from Makeenko–Migdal theory, but for d ≥ 3 it remains a fundamental open problem in mathematical gauge theory.
domain_bridges: free probability and large-N random matrix theory
combinatorial map enumeration and ribbon graphs
Markov processes and heat kernels on compact Lie groups
lattice statistical mechanics and phase transitions
proof_strategy: The paper establishes the rooted heat-kernel master loop equation and proves convergence of the order-truncated trajectory expansion at strong coupling (T > T₀(d)). To extend to all T > 0: (1) Develop uniform-in-T estimates for the trajectory expansion coefficients, leveraging the universal finite-N duality formulas and refined heat-kernel asymptotics that remain valid for small T. (2) Prove convergence of the rooted trajectory expansion for all T > 0 by establishing tighter control on the combinatorial growth of decorated loop observables—specifically, show the expansion is absolutely convergent with radius independent of T. (3) For the weak-coupling regime (small T), exploit the Gaussian limit T → 0 where the theory reduces to a lattice Gaussian free field, and use this as the base of an expansion valid for all T. (4) Bridge strong and weak coupling using monotonicity of Wilson loop expectations in T and real-analyticity of heat-kernel coefficients, establishing a single master field
title: Existence of the Large-N Master Field for Heat-Kernel Yang-Mills on Z^d at All Couplings

description: The misère quotient for a two-step escalation game (m=2) is isomorphic to the order-six monoid ⟨a,b | a²=1, b³=b⟩ with loss set {a, b²}.
proof_strategy: Define the monoid in Lean, compute the misère quotient via backward induction, and prove isomorphism through homomorphism properties and loss set verification
title: Structure of the Misère Quotient for Two-Step Escalation

description: For the exponential sum $S(h,n) = \sum_{a=\lceil n/2 \rceil}^{n} e^{2\pi i h \sqrt{a}}$, the authors prove $\sum_{H/2 \le h \le H} |S(h,n)|^2 \ll_{\varepsilon,\delta} H n^{1+\varepsilon}$ for $H \ge n^{1/2+\delta}$. This conjecture proposes that the $n^\varepsilon$ factor can be replaced by a polylogarithmic factor $(\log n)^c$ for some absolute constant $c \ge 0$, yielding the sharper bound $\sum_{H/2 \le h \le H} |S(h,n)|^2 \le C(\delta) \cdot H \cdot n \cdot (\log n)^c$ for all $H \ge \lceil n^{1/2+\delta}\rceil$. This would constitute a near-optimal second-moment estimate matching the diagonal scale up to polylogarithmic factors.
proof_strategy: Refine the Weyl differencing and van der Corput B-process arguments from the paper with tighter control on off-diagonal contributions. The key improvement would come from replacing power-saving arguments with logarithmic precision via careful saddle-point analysis of the complete exponential sums arising from Poisson summation applied to $e(h\sqrt{a})$ over dyadic subintervals of $[n/2, n]$. One should track how the exponent pairs obtained from the $B^2$-process interact with the moment sum over $h$, exploiting cancellation more finely than the $n^\varepsilon$-losing bound permits.
title: Sharp Second-Moment Bound for Square-Root Exponential Sums with Polylogarithmic Loss

description: This conjecture concerns the exact asymptotic behavior of the saturation number for complete 4-partite graphs, quantifying the minimal edge count required to ensure saturation of saturation levels for $C_4$-free graphs.
proof_strategy: inductive construction combined with probabilistic extremal arguments
title: All minimum $C_4$-saturated multipartite graphs

description: Let k=3 and j>=2 be an even integer, and let f be a primitive elliptic cusp form of weight j+4 for SL_2(Z). For any prime ideal p of the Hecke field Q(f) dividing the algebraic critical value L^alg(j+3, f), there exists a Siegel cusp eigenform F of weight det^3 Sym^j for Sp_2 and a prime ideal P above p such that the spinor L-polynomial congruence L_ell(X, F, Spin) = L_ell(X, f)(1 - ell X)(1 - ell^{j+2} X) mod P holds for all primes ell.
proof_strategy: Extend the Hermitian Klingenstein-Eisenstein lift congruence to the scalar-valued boundary case (k=3) by modifying Mok's endoscopic classification to handle the non-trivial SL_2-factor in the Arthur parameters, and adapting the Selmer-group vanishing arguments as outlined in the paper's discussion of the k=3 boundary.
title: Harder's Conjecture for the Scalar-Valued Hermitian Boundary Case (k=3)

description: For any p-adic field F and any irreducible smooth admissible generic representation π of GL(n, F), the Bessel distribution B_{ℓ₁,ℓ₂} associated to Whittaker functionals is regular: there exists a unique smooth function j defined on a dense open subset of GL(n, F), locally integrable on GL(n, F), such that B_{ℓ₁,ℓ₂}(f) = ∫_{GL(n,F)} j(g)f(g)dg for all Schwartz functions f. This follows from the paper's main result (regularity follows from nontrivial bounds on Kloosterman sums for all Levi subgroups) combined with the known Deligne-Weil bounds on Kloosterman sums for all Levi subgroups of GL(n), which are products of smaller GL(m)'s.
proof_strategy: Apply the paper's conditional regularity theorem (Bessel distributions are regular provided Kloosterman sums for all Levi subgroups have nontrivial bounds) to GL(n). Since every Levi subgroup of GL(n) is isomorphic to a product ∏ GL(mᵢ) with ∑ mᵢ = n, the corresponding Kloosterman sums admit nontrivial bounds by Deligne's estimates from the Riemann hypothesis for varieties over finite fields (Weil II), yielding unconditional regularity for GL(n). The key intermediate step is formalizing the germ expansion of Kloosterman integrals and verifying the nontrivial bound condition for all Levi subgroups.
title: Regularity of Bessel Distributions for Generic Representations of GL(n) over p-adic Fields

description: For every finite graph F with m > 0 edges and n non-isolated vertices, if p ≥ C(n,2)/m, then for every ρ-locally dense graphon W, the L^p norm of the subgraph density function W_F satisfies ||W_F||_{L^p} ≥ ρ^m, where W_F(x₁,...,xₙ) = ∏_{ij∈E(F)} W(xᵢ,xⱼ) and ρ-local density means ∫_{S×S} W ≥ ρ·λ(S)² for all measurable S ⊆ [0,1]. This is the main theorem of the paper, establishing that every graph satisfies an L^p relaxation of the KNRS conjecture at the threshold p = C(n,2)/m.
proof_strategy: Hölder uniformization over vertex relabellings in the spirit of Conlon–Lee: reduce the general case to the edge-transitive case by averaging over graph automorphisms and applying Hölder's inequality to symmetrize, then exploit the positive-semidefinite structure implicit in local density for edge-transitive graphs. Key sub-lemmas include the equivalence between the L^p formulation and the graphon composition formulation, and the comparison principle with edge-transitive KNRS supergraphs.
title: L^p Relaxation of the KNRS Conjecture for Graphons

description: For a prime p ≥ 3 and an integer b ≥ 2 with p ∤ b, if the multiplicative order of b modulo p is l = (p-1)/2^m and p ≡ 1 mod 2^(m+1), then the sum of the base-b digits in one full period of the expansion of 1/p equals (b-1)(p-1)/2^(m+1).
proof_strategy: Define the base-b digit sequence of 1/p using the division algorithm on remainders, a_i = ⌊b * r_i / p⌋ where r_i = b^i mod p. The sum of digits S = Σ a_i can be expressed in terms of the sum of remainders. The condition that the order of b is (p-1)/2^m restricts the remainders to a subgroup of (ℤ/pℤ)×. The congruence p ≡ 1 mod 2^(m+1) ensures that this subgroup is stable under negation modulo p (since l is even and b^(l/2) ≡ -1 mod p), which allows the sum of remainders to be simplified to p*l/2, leading directly to the formula S = (b-1)*l/2 = (b-1)(p-1)/2^(m+1).
title: Digit Sum Formula for Prime Reciprocals with Half-Order Periods

description: The paper establishes that c(s/log s)^{4/3} ≤ F(s) ≤ (1+o(1))s^{3/2}/log s, where F(s) = max{χ(G) : ω(G) ≤ s, g(G̅) ≥ 6}. The conjecture proposes that the true asymptotic growth rate is Θ(s^{3/2}/log s), i.e., the upper bound is tight. Specifically, there exists a constant c > 0 such that for all sufficiently large s, F(s) ≥ c · s^{3/2} / log s, which would close the gap between the exponent 4/3 in the lower bound and 3/2 in the upper bound.
proof_strategy: To prove the lower bound F(s) ≥ c·s^{3/2}/log s, construct an explicit family of graphs G_s with ω(G_s) ≤ s and g(G̅_s) ≥ 6 such that χ(G_s) ≥ c·s^{3/2}/log s. This likely requires probabilistic constructions or algebraic graph families that saturate the complement-girth-6 constraint while maximizing chromatic number relative to clique number. The existing lower bound construction yielding s^{4/3} would need substantial refinement—potentially using blow-ups of Ramsey-type constructions or sparse pseudorandom graphs with controlled complement girth.
title: Asymptotic Growth Rate of the Sivaraman Function F(s)

description: For each integer n ≥ 1, the theta-mode component φ_n(t) of the even Riemann phase kernel equals the action of the differential operator (∂_t² − 1/4) on the explicit function e^{t/2} · e^{−πn²e^{2t}}. This is the key analytic identity underpinning the finite-core Volterra program: it provides an exact same-sign formula decomposing the phase kernel modes into a boundary term and a Volterra tail, and is the foundation for the quotient Schur certificate. Formalization requires the definition of φ_n via the even Riemann kernel Φ, the computation of the second derivative of the explicit exponential, and the verification of the equality as an identity of smooth functions on ℝ.
proof_strategy: First formalize the even Riemann kernel Φ and its phase-mode decomposition into components φ_n. Then define the explicit test function g_n(t) = exp(t/2) · exp(−π·n²·exp(2t)). Compute ∂_t g_n and ∂_t² g_n symbolically using differentiation rules for compositions and products. Subtract (1/4)·g_n to form (∂_t² − 1/4)g_n. The equality φ_n = (∂_t² − 1/4)g_n then follows from the Jacobi-type theta identity and the Poisson summation relation connecting the Riemann kernel to the theta function, rearranged via the heat-equation eigenfunction expansion that produces the second-order operator.
title: Second-order theta-mode identity for the Riemann phase kernel

description: Conjecture: In the game of Halve Nim (where a move consists of either a standard Nim move on a single pile or replacing every pile of size n by ⌊n/2⌋), a position with three piles of sizes (a, b, c) is a P-position if and only if the nim‑sum a ⊕ b ⊕ c equals zero. This extends the known result for two‑pile Halve Nim and the partial result for three‑pile Halve Nim with one pile bounded by ten.
proof_strategy: Proceed by induction on the total number of coins. Show that the Grundy value of a pile of size n is exactly n (i.e., the halving move does not change the nim‑value), using the mex recurrence and the fact that ⌊n/2⌋ < n for n>0. Then the Sprague‑Grundy theorem gives that the Grundy value of a position is the xor of the pile sizes, so P‑positions are precisely those with xor zero. The induction handles the base case (empty position) and the step where either a standard Nim move or a global halving move is considered.
title: Characterization of P-positions in three-pile Halve Nim

description: For the siblings of the coupon collector problem with N coupon types and album index j ≥ 2, the expected number of empty spaces E_p[U_j^N] in sibling j's album at the main collector's completion time is uniquely maximized over all probability distributions p = (p_1, ..., p_N) with p_i > 0 and Σ p_i = 1 by the uniform distribution p_i = 1/N. Moreover, E_p[U_j^N] decreases strictly along every nonconstant ray from the uniform vector in the probability simplex.
proof_strategy: The proof relies on: (1) establishing the Adler-Oren-Ross integral formula for E_p[U_j^N] as a sum of integrals involving the product of survival functions, (2) showing that E_p[U_j^N] is a Schur-convex function of the probability vector p (using the characterization that symmetric convex functions are Schur-convex), and (3) applying the majorization order to conclude that the uniform distribution (which is majorized by all other distributions) maximizes the expectation. The ray-decrease property follows from strict Schur-convexity. Formalization requires building the probability space for the coupon collector, the integral formula, and the Schur-convexity framework.
title: Uniform Distribution Uniquely Maximizes Expected Empty Spaces in Sibling Coupon Collection

catalog_references: Cutoff profiles for colored top-m-to-random shuffles with growing block size
description: The probability that exactly u labels are untouched after k_n independent uniform m_n-subset drawings from n labels converges to the Poisson probability e^{-λ} λ^u / u! whenever the expected number of untouched labels λ_n = n ((n-m_n)/n)^{k_n} → λ ∈ (0, ∞) and the complement size b_n = n - m_n → ∞.
proof_strategy: Compute the factorial moments of the untouched-label statistic E_n by evaluating the expected size of the intersection of r untouched labels, showing they converge to λ^r. By inclusion-exclusion, the probability that exactly u labels are untouched is expressed as an alternating sum involving the probabilities of larger sets of untouched labels. The asymptotic conditions λ_n → λ and b_n → ∞ (equivalently γ_n → 0) ensure that the inclusion-exclusion sum converges to the Poisson probabilities, using the method of moments or direct asymptotic analysis of the binomial coefficients.
title: Poisson Limit for Group-Drawing Coupon Collector

description: Let X be a d-dimensional weighted simplicial complex with distribution π on X(d). If there exists α > 0 such that every link X_σ for σ ∈ X(d-2) satisfies a KKL property with parameter α — meaning for every g : X_σ(1) → ℝ, max_{v ∈ X_σ(0)} Inf_v(g) ≥ α · Var(g) — then X globally satisfies a KKL property with the same parameter α: for every f : X(d) → ℝ, max_{σ ∈ X(d-2)} Inf_σ(f) ≥ α · Var(f). This captures the paper's central local-to-global principle: the KKL phenomenon on a simplicial complex is inherited from its links.
proof_strategy: Decompose global variance and influence via the link structure. Show that Var(f) on X(d) can be written as a weighted sum of local variances on links, and that the global max influence is at least the local max influence at each link, using the local KKL property at each link X_σ. The key step is establishing that the influence Inf_σ(f) on the global complex dominates the corresponding influence in the link X_σ, possibly up to dimension-dependent factors that cancel due to the uniform transfer of the KKL parameter α.
title: Local-to-Global KKL Transfer for Simplicial Complexes

description: For any connected graph G with an edge partition P of E(G) into t classes, let A be the cycle-class parity matrix over GF(2) constructed from P. The induced quotient labeling ℓ: V(G) → (Z/2Z)^(t − rank(A)) satisfies d_G(u,v) ≥ d_H(ℓ(u), ℓ(v)) for all u,v ∈ V(G), where H is the hypercube Cayley graph on (Z/2Z)^(t − rank(A)). That is, the labeling never stretches distances—it can fail to be isometric only by shortcuts (contracting distances), never by stretching them.
proof_strategy: Show that each edge of G maps to an edge of H under the quotient labeling (by construction of the labeling from the edge partition), so every path in G maps to a path of equal or shorter length in H. The key step is proving that the GF(2) quotient construction preserves adjacency: if uv ∈ E(G) and uv lies in partition class i, then ℓ(u) and ℓ(v) differ in exactly the coordinate corresponding to the image of class i in the quotient. The non-stretching then follows by taking d_G(u,v) as the infimum over all path lengths, which bound the Hamming distance of the labels from below.
title: No-Stretching Property of GF(2) Quotient Labelings from Edge Partitions

description: For all d ≥ 1, the maximum number of equiangular lines in ℝ^d with common angle arccos(1/3) satisfies N_{1/3}(d) ≤ max{28, 2(d − 1)}. This is a special case of Balla's conjecture where the spectral radius order κ₁ = 2 (witnessed by K₂), making the bound reduce to max{(1−1/9)(1−2/9)/(2/81), ⌊2(d−1)/1⌋} = max{28, 2(d−1)}.
proof_strategy: First establish κ₁ = 2 by showing K₂ has spectral radius 1 and no 1-vertex graph has spectral radius 1. Then use the relative bound / Lemmens-Seidel framework: given a set of equiangular lines with angle arccos(1/3), form the Gram matrix M with diagonal 1 and off-diagonal ±1/3. The eigenvalue structure of M combined with the spectral radius order constraint yields the linear upper bound 2(d−1) for d ≥ 15, and the absolute bound gives 28 for small d.
title: Balla's Conjecture for α = 1/3

catalog_references: Paper: Multiplicative functions additive on partitions of $2k$ nonzero squares
description: For k=3, any multiplicative function f : ℕ → ℂ that is 3-additive on the set E₂ of sums of two nonzero squares and satisfies f(2) ≠ 0 must be the identity function. Formally, if f is multiplicative, f(2) ≠ 0, and f(x₁² + x₂² + x₃² + x₄² + x₅² + x₆²) = f(x₁² + x₂²) + f(x₃² + x₄²) + f(x₅² + x₆²) for all positive integers x₁, ..., x₆, then f(n) = n for all n ∈ ℕ.
proof_strategy: Establish the result by first proving base cases for small numbers and primes. Use the multiplicative property along with the 3-additive condition on E₂ to show f(p) = p for all primes p. Then extend multiplicatively to all natural numbers, carefully utilizing the f(2) ≠ 0 condition to rule out the zero-like exceptional cases.
title: k=3 Additive Uniqueness of Multiplicative Functions on Sums of Two Nonzero Squares

description: For any set P of n ≥ 3 points in general position (no three collinear) in ℝ², the number of labeled plane graphs on P is at least the number of labeled plane graphs on n points in convex position. This formalizes the conjecture that, among all n-point configurations in general position, convex position yields the fewest plane graphs. The paper proves that configurations with convex hull of size O(n/log n) have Ω(12.24^n) plane graphs, strictly more than the ~11.65^n achieved by convex position, providing strong evidence for this conjecture.
proof_strategy: Use the vertex potential framework from the paper to show that interior points (not on the convex hull) strictly increase the number of plane graphs relative to convex position. The potential φ(v) = deg(v) + vis(v) captures the local combinatorial richness at each vertex. The strategy would be: (1) establish that the expected potential of an interior vertex in a random plane graph strictly exceeds that of a hull vertex, (2) show this potential gap translates to a multiplicative increase in the total count of plane graphs, and (3) induct on the number of interior points, reducing to the base case of convex position. A key lemma would be that moving a hull point to the interior (while maintaining general position) strictly increases the plane graph count.
title: Convex Position Minimizes Plane Graphs

description: The Berry-Keating Hamiltonian H_BK = (xp + px)/2 on L²(ℝ⁺), when equipped with a suitable self-adjoint extension satisfying the appropriate boundary condition, has spectrum {λ_n} such that λ_n = t_n² + 1/4, where ρ_n = 1/2 + it_n ranges over the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. This would verify the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture for this specific operator and imply the Riemann Hypothesis, since self-adjoint operators have real eigenvalues, forcing all t_n to be real and thus all ρ_n to lie on Re(s) = 1/2.
domain_bridges: spectral theory of unbounded operators ↔ analytic number theory
quantum Hamiltonian spectrum ↔ Riemann zeta zero distribution
proof_strategy: 1) Define H_BK = (xp+px)/2 rigorously as an unbounded operator on L²(ℝ⁺) with domain specified by boundary conditions. 2) Prove existence and uniqueness of the self-adjoint extension using von Neumann deficiency index theory. 3) Compute the trace of the resolvent Tr((H_BK - s(s-1))⁻¹) via the Gutzwiller trace formula for this Hamiltonian. 4) Show via analytic continuation that the spectral zeta function ζ_{H_BK}(s) equals the Riemann xi function ξ(s). 5) Conclude spectral correspondence via the equality of zeta-regularized spectral determinants: det_ζ(H_BK - s(s-1)I) = ξ(s).
title: Berry-Keating Hamiltonian Spectrum Corresponds to Riemann Zeta Non-Trivial Zeros

description: For every odd prime p and integer r with 1 ≤ r ≤ p-1, the maximum size of a symmetric set S = -S ⊆ ℤ_p \ {0} such that the Cayley graph Cay(ℤ_p, S) is K_{r+1}-free equals p - 1 - 2⌊p/(r+1)⌋. This is the main theorem of the paper, established via a polynomial method.
proof_strategy: Formalize Cayley graphs over ZMod p, symmetric connection sets, and K_{r+1}-freeness. Prove the lower bound by showing Cay(ℤ_p, ℤ_p \ D_0) is K_{r+1}-free where D_0 = {0, ±1, ..., ±⌊p/(r+1)⌋}. Prove the upper bound via the polynomial method: for a K_{r+1}-free Cayley graph with connection set S, construct a nonzero polynomial of bounded degree vanishing on the complement D = ℤ_p \ S, then use the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz or degree-counting to derive |S| ≤ p - 1 - 2⌊p/(r+1)⌋.
title: Cayley-Turán number of complete graphs over prime cyclic groups

description: For a real quadratic field K = ℚ(√D) with D > 1 squarefree, the octonary diagonal form f = x₁² + x₂² + x₃² + x₄² + ε₊(x₅² + x₆² + x₇² + x₈²) over the ring of integers 𝓞ₖ is universal if and only if the Blomer-Kala invariant M_D (the cardinality of the set S₀ of indecomposable totally positive integers modulo totally positive units) equals 1.
proof_strategy: First, formalize the Blomer-Kala invariant M_D as a continued fraction sum evaluating the cardinality of the set S₀ of indecomposable totally positive integers. Next, formalize the universality of the octonary form f. The backward direction (M_D = 1 implies universality) requires demonstrating that the Blomer-Kala universal 8M_D-variable construction collapses exactly to f, and then verifying that M_D = 1 implies D belongs to one of the two classified families (D = n²-1 or D = n²-4), for which universality holds. The forward direction (universality implies M_D = 1) requires demonstrating that if M_D > 1, the form f fails to represent certain indecomposable elements in S₀.
title: Universality of Kim's Octonary Form via the Blomer-Kala Invariant

description: The Croot-Lev half-threshold problem, now resolved by the authors, establishes that in a 2-torsion-free abelian group G, if r_A(d) ≥ |A|/2 for all d ∈ A−A, then A is either a single coset or a union of two cosets of some finite subgroup H. This conjecture proposes the natural generalization to the 1/3 threshold: if r_A(d) ≥ |A|/3 for all d ∈ A−A, then A is contained in at most 3 cosets of some finite subgroup H. The bound k on the number of cosets scales with the reciprocal of the threshold, and the 2-torsion-free hypothesis remains essential (as the authors' counterexamples in F_2^{2r+1} also violate the 1/3-threshold coset conclusion).
proof_strategy: Extend the authors' Kneser quotient reduction and Kemperman critical-pair framework from the 1/2-threshold to the 1/3-threshold regime. The key steps would be: (1) Establish a Kneser-type lower bound for |A−A| when the 1/3-popular condition holds, showing that the deficit |A−A| − |A| is controlled by the Kneser quotient; (2) Classify the critical-pair configurations that achieve equality or near-equality in the 1/3-threshold regime, showing that the deficit forces a 3-coset structure; (3) Handle the case where A−A is a subgroup separately (where A is a single coset) versus the case where A−A is not a subgroup (where the Kemperman analysis forces A into at most 3 cosets).
