The 2-torsion-free assumption is used in the Kemperman step to ensure that the critical-pair classification yields coset structures rather than the exotic configurations the authors construct in F_2^{2r+1}.
title: Third-Threshold Coset Structure in 2-Torsion-Free Abelian Groups

description: For any finite simple digraph G, the cycle rank of G is less than or equal to the size of a minimum feedback vertex set of G. This inequality establishes a fundamental bound between the depth parameter cycle rank and the width parameter feedback vertex set, which is tight for tournaments (a subclass of semi-complete digraphs studied in the paper) and provides structural intuition for FPT algorithms related to cycle rank and feedback sets.
proof_strategy: Induction on the size k of a minimum feedback vertex set S. Base case k=0: G is acyclic, so crank(G) = 0. If G is not strongly connected, crank(G) is the maximum cycle rank over its strongly connected components, each of which has a feedback vertex set of size <= k, so the bound holds by the inductive hypothesis. If G is strongly connected and k>0, then |V(G)| >= 2 (since simple digraphs have no self-loops and k>0 implies a cycle exists). Removing any vertex v in S reduces the minimum feedback vertex set size of G-v to k-1. By the recursive definition of cycle rank, crank(G) = 1 + min_u crank(G-u) <= 1 + crank(G-v) <= 1 + (k-1) = k.
title: Cycle Rank is Bounded by Minimum Feedback Vertex Set Size

description: Let A₁, …, Aᵣ be simple abelian varieties over Q̄ such that no two are isogenous, let X = A₁ × ⋯ × Aᵣ, and let f: X → X be an endomorphism with a Zariski dense orbit. Then there exists a number field K such that every (f,K)-transversal is Zariski dense in X. This extends the Pasten-Silverman S-DOT result (which covers only the case r=1, i.e., geometrically simple abelian varieties) to products of pairwise non-isogenous simples, and strengthens the current paper's W-DOT result (which only guarantees the existence of some dense transversal) to the universality of density for all transversals.
proof_strategy: Decompose the endomorphism f on X = A₁ × ⋯ × Aᵣ into component maps fᵢⱼ: Aⱼ → Aᵢ using the structure of End(X) ≅ ⊕ End(Aᵢ) when the Aᵢ are pairwise non-isogenous. Apply the Pasten-Silverman S-DOT result on each simple factor to obtain independent transversality, then show that the product structure forces any global transversal to project onto Zariski dense subsets of each factor, yielding Zariski density in the product. The key difficulty is ensuring no transversal can concentrate on a proper closed subset that projects surjectively onto each factor.
title: Strong Dense Orbit Transversality for Products of Non-Isogenous Simple Abelian Varieties

description: An optimal equidistant binary code E(n, d*, m*) of length n >= 3 exists if and only if a corresponding symmetric balanced incomplete block design exists. Specifically, for n ≡ 3 mod 4, it is equivalent to a Hadamard matrix of order n+1; for n ≡ 0 mod 4, a Hadamard matrix of order n; for n ≡ 1 mod 4, a (2u^2+2u+1, u^2, u(u-1)/2)-SBIBD; and for n ≡ 2 mod 4, it is equivalent to one of two specific subcases of SBIBDs, including the previously missed subcase identified in the paper.
proof_strategy: Proceed by case analysis on n mod 4. For each case, establish the bounds d* and m* using the Fisher-type inequality and the Plotkin bound. Then, construct the bidirectional equivalence between the optimal equidistant code and the corresponding symmetric design by mapping codewords to blocks and vice versa, paying special attention to the exhaustive classification of the two possible subcases when n ≡ 2 mod 4.
title: Complete Characterization of Optimal Equidistant Binary Codes via Symmetric Designs

description: Let p be an odd prime, K/Q_p an unramified quadratic extension, and ρ̄: Gal(K̄/K) → GL₂(F) an irreducible mod p Galois representation (F a finite extension of F_p). Using perfectoid geometry on the Drinfeld tower, one associates to ρ̄ an infinite-dimensional smooth mod p representation Π(ρ̄) of the Borel subgroup B_K = {(a b; 0 1) : a ∈ K^×, b ∈ K} ⊂ GL₂(K). The conjecture states that Π(ρ̄) is irreducible as a smooth representation of B_K. This is a necessary condition for Π(ρ̄) to equal the restriction of the (conjectural) supersingular representation π of GL₂(K) corresponding to ρ̄, which is the central hope expressed in the paper for resolving the locality question.
proof_strategy: Adapt Colmez's strategy for K=Q_p: use the (φ,Γ)-module structure of D(ρ̄) to control the B_K-submodules of Π(ρ̄). For K=Q_p, irreducibility of the associated B-representation follows from the compatibility between the (φ,Γ)-module action and the B-action via Fontaine's cyclotomic module. For quadratic K, one must leverage the additional perfectoid structure of the Drinfeld tower (specifically, the action of the larger group GL₂(O_K) on the pro-étale cover) to show that any B_K-stable subspace is forced to be either 0 or the whole space. The key difficulty is that the (φ,Γ)-module for K≠Q_p carries richer structure (Γ ≅ O_K^× rather than Z_p^×), and the interplay between this and the B_K-action via the perfectoid diamond must be controlled.
title: Irreducibility of the perfectoid Borel representation for quadratic unramified extensions

description: For every sufficiently large prime p, every nonzero residue class modulo p is represented by a product of two primes each at most p. This is Erdős's original conjecture that motivates the paper's ternary result; the paper proves the ternary analogue (every class is a product of three primes) and shows a positive proportion of classes are products of two primes, but the full binary conjecture remains open.
proof_strategy: Extend the multiplicative dense-model and transference framework of Matomäki–Teräväinen (as generalized in this paper to narrow ray class groups) from the ternary to the binary setting. The key obstacle is showing that the product set P_p · P_p equals all of (Z/pZ)* rather than merely having large cardinality. This requires stronger character sum bounds or a structural understanding of when a product set of primes in a finite abelian group is surjective, going beyond the positive-density results currently achievable.
title: Erdős Binary Product Conjecture for Primes

description: For the Fibonacci numeration system $U$ with standard initial conditions (where $u_0=1, u_1=2$), the topological group $\mathbb{Z}_U$, constructed as the completion of $\mathbb{Z}$ under the pseudo-valuation $\nu_U$, is continuously isomorphic to the circle group $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. This is a specific instance of the paper's main theorem where the Pisot number is the golden ratio (unimodular, degree 2).
proof_strategy: Define the Fibonacci numeration system and its pseudo-valuation, construct the completion $\mathbb{Z}_U$ as a topological group, define the evaluation map $\tau_U$ using the non-trivial Galois conjugate of the golden ratio ($\phi' = 1-\phi$), and prove it is a continuous group isomorphism to $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.
title: Fibonacci Numeration Group is the Circle Group

description: For every oriented graph D (a finite directed simple graph without loops or digons) with minimum out-degree δ⁺(D) ≤ 7, there exists a Seymour vertex v ∈ V(D) satisfying |N⁺⁺(v)| ≥ |N⁺(v)|, where N⁺(v) is the first out-neighborhood and N⁺⁺(v) is the second out-neighborhood. This formalizes the main theorem of the paper, which improves the Kaneko–Locke threshold from 6 to 7. The stronger local version is also conjectured: if s is a vertex of minimum out-degree, then a Seymour vertex exists in {s} ∪ N⁺(s) ∪ N⁺⁺(s).
proof_strategy: The formalization proceeds in three stages: (1) Define oriented graphs, out-neighborhoods N⁺(v), second out-neighborhoods N⁺⁺(v), and Seymour vertices in Lean 4, together with the minimum out-degree predicate. (2) Formalize the paper's local reduction lemmas, which transform an arbitrary counterexample into a finite set of irreducible obstruction configurations—these are purely mathematical arguments amenable to direct formalization. (3) For each finite obstruction model, extract the CP-SAT infeasibility certificate logs produced by OR-Tools and verify them in Lean as explicit proof terms (mirroring the approach of the Flyspeck project for the Kepler conjecture), establishing that no obstruction exists. The combination of (2) and (3) yields the main theorem.
title: Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture holds for oriented graphs with minimum out-degree at most 7

description: The polynomial prefactor in the bound for sunflower-free families can be eliminated entirely. Specifically, there exists an absolute constant C > 0 such that for all n ≥ 1 and all 3-sunflower-free families F ⊆ 2^{[n]}, |F| ≤ C · (3/2^{2/3})^n. This would strengthen the paper's O(n^{1/6}(3/2^{2/3})^n) bound by removing the polynomial factor, and would follow if i-triangular tensor methods could be applied with arbitrarily large tensor orders to drive the polynomial factor to a constant.
proof_strategy: Construct a hierarchy of i-triangular tensor encodings for sunflower-free families with increasing tensor order k and triangularity parameter i, applying the generalized slice-rank lemma to drive the polynomial exponent toward 0. Alternatively, develop a recursive composition of the 1-triangular construction where the output of one layer feeds into the next, achieving polylogarithmic or constant prefactor.
title: Polynomial-Free Sunflower Bound

description: There exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every d-regular n-vertex graph G (with 1 ≤ d ≤ n−1), there is a spanning subgraph H of G in which for each degree i ∈ {0, 1, …, d}, the number of vertices of degree exactly i in H is at least c·n/(d+1). This extends the paper's result—which requires d = o(n) and achieves (1−ε)·n/(d+1)—by asking whether a weaker constant-fraction guarantee holds uniformly for all d, removing the d = o(n) restriction entirely.
proof_strategy: For small d, a random subgraph (each edge included with probability 1/2) yields near-uniform degree distribution via concentration. For large d (linear in n), the binomial degree distribution concentrates around d/2 with width O(√d), so most degrees cluster and the random approach fails to cover all d+1 degree values. A hybrid strategy might combine: (1) random sparsification to reduce effective degree, (2) deterministic local adjustments (edge swaps) to redistribute degrees, or (3) algebraic methods (e.g., polynomial interpolation via inclusion matrices) to guarantee each degree class is populated. The key obstacle is ensuring low-degree vertices (near 0) and high-degree vertices (near d) coexist when d is large.
title: Universal constant-fraction nearly-uniform degree distribution in spanning subgraphs

description: For each integer k and complex parameters (mₗ, mᵣ), the slash action |_{k,[mₗ,mᵣ]} defined on pseudodifferential operators on the Jacobi upper half space—via the decomposition of cocycles into left and right parts α_{k-n,mₗ} and α_{mᵣ}—satisfies the right group action axioms: (1) φ ∂ⁿ |_{k,[mₗ,mᵣ]} e = φ ∂ⁿ for the identity e ∈ G, and (2) (φ ∂ⁿ |_{k,[mₗ,mᵣ]} g₁) |_{k,[mₗ,mᵣ]} g₂ = φ ∂ⁿ |_{k,[mₗ,mᵣ]} (g₁g₂) for all g₁, g₂ ∈ G. This is the foundational verification (referenced as checked directly in the paper) upon which the equivariant isomorphism between invariant pseudodifferential operators and Jacobi forms depends.
proof_strategy: Define the extended real Jacobi group G as a semidirect product, formalize the cocycles α_{k,mₗ} and α_{mᵣ} and their composition properties under group multiplication, then verify the two group action axioms by direct computation using the cocycle identity and the compatibility of the β-factor (cτ+d) with the derivative ∂ under coordinate change z ↦ z∘g.
title: Slash action of the Jacobi group on pseudodifferential operators is a well-defined right group action

description: For every convex polytope P ⊆ ℝ_{>0}^k with vertices in ℚ^k, the sieve integral I(P) = ∫_P (dt₁⋯dt_k)/(t₁⋯t_k) is a finite ℚ-linear combination of logarithms of positive rational numbers. This formalizes the algebraic nature of the outputs produced by the LattE-based computation method proposed in the paper, asserting that the transcendental content of sieve integrals over rational polytopes is entirely captured by log-rational expressions.
proof_strategy: Use Brion's theorem to decompose the integral I(P) as a sum over vertex cones of P. For each vertex cone C with rational apex, apply the change of variables t_i = exp(u_i) to transform ∫_C dt/(t₁⋯t_k) into ∫_{log C} du, where log C is an unbounded polyhedral cone. Then apply Barvinok's decomposition of log C into unimodular cones, and evaluate each unimodular cone integral as a rational-linear combination of products of rational reciprocals and logarithms of rationals, using the iterated integration formula for monomial integrals over simplicial cones.
title: Sieve Integral Rational Polytope Algebraicity Conjecture

description: The paper proves that for a multiset P of n real numbers summing to zero (not all zero) and 1 ≤ k < n, the Shannon entropy of X_P (the sum of k elements sampled uniformly without replacement from P) satisfies H(X_P) ≥ H(Ber(k/n)). This conjecture asserts that the same inequality holds for Rényi entropy of order 2 (collision entropy): H₂(X_P) ≥ H₂(Ber(k/n)), equivalently, the collision probability of X_P is at most (k/n)² + (1−k/n)². Equality is achieved when P consists of one large positive value and n−1 equal negative values (e.g., P = {(n−1), −1, …, −1}), since then X_P is a scaled Bernoulli variable. The conjecture fails for min-entropy (α → ∞), as demonstrated by P = {1,1,−1,−1} with k=2 where max probability = 2/3 > 1/2, so the threshold α ≤ 2 is natural.
proof_strategy: Adapt the Schur-concavity and majorization arguments from the paper. The key steps would be: (1) Show that H₂(X_P) is Schur-concave in the probability vector of X_P; (2) Reduce to the case where P has a specific extremal structure (e.g., two-valued multisets) using majorization; (3) For two-valued multisets {a,…,a,b,…,b} with ka+(n−k)b=0, X_P is a scaled hypergeometric variable—prove that H₂ is minimized when the hypergeometric reduces to Bernoulli (i.e., when one value appears exactly once); (4) Alternatively, use the data-processing inequality for Rényi divergence under suitable channels, extending the information-theoretic approach.
title: Entropic MMS for Rényi Entropy of Order 2 (Collision Entropy)

description: Conjecture that any C4-free graph of diameter 2 without universal vertices and maximum degree at least 17 is not 3-colorable, formalizing the main structural result of the paper.
proof_strategy: Define the graph properties (C4-freeness, diameter-2, absence of universal vertices, max degree >= 17) in Lean. Proceed by contradiction by assuming a valid 3-coloring exists, then derive a contradiction using the structural properties of the neighborhood of a vertex with degree >= 17. Specifically, exploit the fact that the neighborhood of any vertex in a C4-free graph induces a matching, and use the diameter-2 condition to show that the coloring constraints force a contradiction.
title: Non-3-Colorability of C4-Free Diameter-2 Graphs with Maximum Degree at least 17

description: Let $q_n \ge 2$ be a sequence of integers and $\psi$ a monotonic function. Define $W_Q(\psi)$ as the set of $x \in [0,1)$ such that $x - \omega_n(x) < \psi(n)/Q_n$ for infinitely many $n$, where $\omega_n(x)$ is the $n$-th partial sum of the Cantor series expansion and $Q_n = \prod_{i=1}^n q_i$. Define the exact approximation set $E_Q(\psi) = W_Q(\psi) \setminus \bigcup_{0<c<1} W_Q(c\psi)$. If $\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\log q_n}{\log Q_n} = 0$, then the Hausdorff dimension of $E_Q(\psi)$ is $1/\lambda$, where $\lambda = \liminf_{n\to\infty} \frac{-\log \psi(n)}{\log Q_n}$.
proof_strategy: Adapt Bugeaud's techniques to the non-autonomous dynamical system setting: establish the upper bound for the Hausdorff dimension using a standard $s$-dimensional Hausdorff measure covering argument, and establish the lower bound by constructing a suitable Cantor set inside the exact approximation set and applying a non-autonomous mass transference principle.
title: Exact Hausdorff Dimension of Exact Approximation Sets in Cantor Series Expansions

description: For every odd prime p, there exists a constant C(p) such that for all n ≥ 1, there exists a complete 3-AP-free subset of F_p^n of cardinality at most C(p) · p^{⌈n/2⌉}. This conjectures that the trivial counting lower bound Ω(p^{n/2}) on the minimum size a(3-AP, F_p^n) is asymptotically tight, improving the paper's upper bound of O(n^{1+ε} · p^{n/2}) by removing the n^{1+ε} factor. The cyclic group analogue is resolved in the paper with the tight O(√m) bound, and the two-dimensional case F_p^2 is known to admit complete 3-AP-free sets of size O(p) = O(p^{2/2}), so the conjecture is consistent with all known cases.
proof_strategy: Adapt the flexible binary interval block technique from the cyclic group construction to vector spaces. The cyclic group result achieves the tight O(√m) bound using subset-sum sets of flexible digits satisfying 2S_i+1 ≤ d_{i+1} ≤ 3S_i+1, yielding both (2,-1)-avoiding and interval-saturating properties simultaneously. For vector spaces, the paper's construction uses two-sided complete quadratic graphs over subfield flags followed by a padding argument that introduces the n^{1+ε} factor. The key is to replace this padding with a more efficient mechanism—either refine the quadratic graph construction to achieve saturation with only O(p^{n/2}) vertices, or develop a direct-product mechanism analogous to the cyclic group case that avoids dimensional overhead by leveraging the nested subfield structure more directly.
title: Tight Square-Root Bound for Complete 3-AP-Free Sets in Finite Vector Spaces

description: For all positive integers n and r, the basic r-symmetric tropical polynomials of degree at most n separate the orbits of the symmetric group S_n acting on R^{n×r} by row permutations. Formally: for any two matrices A, B ∈ R^{n×r}, if p_α(A) = p_α(B) for every multi-index α ∈ Z_{≥0}^r with |α| ≤ n, then there exists a permutation σ ∈ S_n such that B is obtained from A by permuting rows via σ. Here p_α(M) = max over all tuples (S_1,...,S_r) of pairwise disjoint subsets of {1,...,n} with |S_j| = α_j, of the sum Σ_{j=1}^r Σ_{i∈S_j} M_{ij}, interpreted in the max-plus (tropical) semiring. This resolves in full a conjecture of Kubo (2019) and yields a separating set of size C(n+r,r), far smaller than Derksen's general construction of nr + (nr)!/n! invariants.
proof_strategy: The proof identifies each p_α with the optimal value of an assignment/transportation problem (selecting α_j rows for each column j, maximizing total weight), then shows the dual transportation problem uniquely determines the multiset via an explicit greedy recovery algorithm. Formalization strategy: (1) define the max-plus semiring and tropical polynomials in Lean; (2) formalize the transportation/assignment problem and strong duality for it; (3) prove that equal p_α values for all α imply equal dual solutions; (4) construct the row-by-row recovery algorithm and prove it inverts the map from orbits to invariant vectors. The key combinatorial lemma is that the transportation polytope's dual uniquely encodes the sorted row data.
title: Basic r-Symmetric Tropical Polynomials Separate S_n Orbits

description: Let $X$ be a smooth projective toric variety of dimension $n \ge 2$, and let $L$ be a basepoint-free line bundle on $X$. The Song-Zhu conjecture posits that if the intersection number $L \cdot C \ge n - 1 + p$ for every $T$-invariant curve $C$ on $X$, then $L$ satisfies Property $N_p$. This removes the uniform unimodularity and Thomsen stratification conditions required by the paper's main theorem, providing a purely intersection-theoretic criterion for the linearity of syzygies.
proof_strategy: Prove that the uniform unimodularity condition and the Thomsen stratification intersection-number condition are automatically satisfied for any smooth projective toric variety under the intersection positivity assumption $L \cdot C \ge n - 1 + p$, thereby reducing the conjecture to the paper's main theorem; alternatively, employ direct combinatorial analysis of the associated lattice polytope's Ehrhart theory and its relation to the minimal free resolution of the section ring.
title: Song-Zhu Conjecture on Property N_p for Toric Varieties

description: For a connected orientable hypermap H = (σ, α) with medial map M(H), an all-crossing direction Φ of M(H) exists if and only if every cycle of α has even length. This conjecture connects the paper's novel obstruction (all hyperedges must have even length for any bipartite partial dual to exist) with the paper's main bipartite characterization (H^{E'} is bipartite iff E' = C(Φ) for some all-crossing direction Φ), yielding a complete existence criterion: a bipartite partial dual exists iff all hyperedges have even length.
proof_strategy: The 'only if' direction follows from the paper's obstruction result: if an all-crossing direction exists, then C(Φ) bipartitizes, so all hyperedges must have even length. The 'if' direction requires constructing an all-crossing direction of M(H) from the even-length condition on α-cycles, likely by inductively assigning crossing directions at each medial vertex and using the even-length constraint to ensure local consistency propagates globally.
title: All-Crossing Directions Exist iff All Hyperedges Have Even Length

description: The set of positive integers that admit exactly one representation in the form p + F_{2^k} + F_q, where p and q are primes and k is a nonnegative integer, has positive lower asymptotic density. This extends the main theorem of the paper—which establishes positive lower density for the representable set—by paralleling recent uniqueness results for related Romanoff-type problems.
proof_strategy: Adapt the circle method and sieve techniques used by Wang and Chen for the uniqueness of p+F_k representations, combined with the density arguments for mixed sparse sequences from Chen and Xu, to show that the minor arc contribution does not overwhelm the major arcs, ensuring that a positive proportion of integers have exactly one representation.
title: Uniqueness of Representations as p + F_{2^k} + F_q

description: The paper proves Harder's conjecture on spinor L-polynomial congruences between elliptic cusp forms and Siegel cusp forms of degree two for all k ≥ 4 and even j ≥ 2, by way of Hermitian automorphic forms on U_{2,2}. The case k = 3 is excluded because the Hermitian weight becomes scalar-valued (det^{j/2+2} ⊠ det^{j/2+2}) and Arthur parameters may involve a non-trivial SL_2-factor, requiring separate treatment. The conjecture is that Harder's L-polynomial congruence still holds for k = 3: given a primitive elliptic cusp form f ∈ S_{2k+j-2}(SL_2(Z)) with k=3 and even j ≥ 2, and a prime ideal 𝔭 of Q(f) dividing the algebraic critical value L^alg(k+j, f), there exists a Siegel cusp eigenform F ∈ S_{det^k Sym^j}(Sp_2) and a prime ideal 𝔓 above 𝔭 such that L_ℓ(X, F, Spin) ≡ L_ℓ(X, f)(1 − ℓ^{k-2}X)(1 − ℓ^{k+j-1}X) mod 𝔓 for every prime ℓ.
proof_strategy: Extend the paper's Hermitian framework to k=3 by analyzing the scalar-valued boundary case in Mok's endoscopic classification for U_{2,2}, where the Arthur parameter may involve a non-trivial SL_2-factor. The key steps are: (1) classify the relevant Arthur parameters for the scalar weight det^{j/2+2} ⊠ det^{j/2+2} on U_{2,2}, handling possible non-trivial SL_2-factors; (2) verify the Klingen-Eisenstein congruence still produces a non-zero Hermitian cusp form in this case; (3) apply Skinner's Galois representations and Selmer-group vanishing arguments adapted to the new infinitesimal character data.
title: Harder's congruence for the scalar-valued boundary case k=3

description: For any irreducible admissible generic representation π of a split reductive group G over a p-adic field F, the Whittaker Bessel distribution B_{ℓ₁,ℓ₂} is regular. That is, there exists a unique locally integrable function j on G, which is smooth on a dense open subset of G, such that B_{ℓ₁,ℓ₂}(f) = ∫_G j(g)f(g)dg for all Schwartz functions f. This conjecture is implied by the paper's main theorem provided that Kloosterman sums for all Levi subgroups of G have nontrivial bounds.
proof_strategy: Formalize p-adic split reductive groups and their Levi subgroups, then establish nontrivial bounds for Kloosterman sums on these subgroups. Subsequently, formalize the germ expansion of Kloosterman integrals as constructed in the paper, and finally deduce the regularity of the Bessel distribution by demonstrating that the expansion yields a locally integrable function representing the distribution.
title: Regularity of Whittaker Bessel Distributions for Split Reductive Groups

description: For any graph F with m > 0 edges and n non-isolated vertices, there exists a ρ-locally dense graphon W such that t(F, W^{∘p}) < ρ^{pm} whenever p < binom(n,2)/m. This would establish that the exponent bound in the L^p-form of the KNRS conjecture is essentially tight.
proof_strategy: Construct extremal graphons violating the inequality using step-function approximations and analyze the limiting behavior as p approaches the threshold from below. Employ variational methods and duality arguments in L^p spaces.
title: Sharpness of the L^p Threshold for KNRS Relaxation

description: Let p be a prime, b an integer ≥ 2 such that p does not divide b. If the multiplicative order of b modulo p is (p-1)/2, and p ≡ 1 mod 4, then the sum of the digits of one period of the base-b expansion of 1/p is (b-1)(p-1)/4.
proof_strategy: Define the sequence of digits in the base-b expansion of 1/p. Show that they are given by the integer division of b by p times the sequence of remainders. Use the fact that the remainders cycle through the elements of the subgroup of index 2 in (Z/pZ)*. Since p ≡ 1 mod 4, -1 is in this subgroup, which implies that the digits can be paired as (d, b-1-d). The sum of each pair is b-1, and there are (p-1)/4 pairs, giving a total sum of (b-1)(p-1)/4.
title: Sum of digits of 1/p for half-period length and p ≡ 1 mod 4

description: Establishes that the optimal χ-bounding function F(3) for the class of graphs whose complements have girth at least 6 is exactly 4. This means that any finite simple graph with clique number at most 3 and complement girth at least 6 has chromatic number at most 4, and there exists such a graph where this bound is tight.
proof_strategy: Analyze the structural properties of graphs with clique number at most 3 and complement girth at least 6. Show that such graphs cannot exceed a certain order or must belong to a restricted family where the chromatic number bound can be systematically verified, likely leveraging Ramsey-type bounds and exhaustive case analysis on small vertex counts.
title: Exact Value of Sivaraman's Function F at 3

description: Establish an upper bound on the sum of annihilation number and residue for nontrivial connected graphs in terms of maximum degree and Caro-Wei sum, generalizing the annihilation inequality to support new conjectures.
proof_strategy: Inductive analysis of degree sequences combined with probabilistic averaging over regular graph constructions, leveraging the Caro-Wei sum's averaging property to establish termination conditions for the Havel-Hakimi process.
title: Enumerative Bound on Annihilation-Residue Sum for Connected Graphs

description: The Weyl symbol σ_Φ derived from the even Riemann kernel Φ satisfies the Kastler–Loupias–Miracle-Sole (KLM) condition: for all N ∈ ℕ and all phase-space points z₁,…,zₙ ∈ ℂ, the N×N Hermitian matrix with entries M_{ij} = σ_Φ((z_i+z_j)/2) · exp(i·Im(z̄_i·z_j)/2) is positive semi-definite. This is the central positivity conjecture in the finite-core Volterra reduction program for the Riemann phase kernel. It has been verified in all numerical tests performed and constitutes the paper's stated 'immediate analytic target.' A proof would establish the Weyl-positivity certificate for the normalized model, leaving only the quotient-to-original Weyl lift and uniform ω-coverage as remaining external bridges to RH.
proof_strategy: Define the even Riemann kernel Φ via the Jacobi theta function and its Mellin-type phase transform. Compute the Weyl symbol σ_Φ from the phase kernel using the second-order theta-mode identity φ_n(t) = (∂²_t − 1/4)(e^{t/2}·e^{−πn²e^{2t}}). Establish KLM positivity by showing σ_Φ decomposes as a sum/integral of positive-type terms, leveraging the same-sign finite-core formulae and the Volterra boundary-plus-tail representation. The quotient Schur factorization of the normalized full-Φ model provides a structural certificate template: if the normalized model's active trace-range, source-inactive domination, and Douglas/Moore–Penrose Schur conditions close, then the KLM condition reduces to verifying positivity of the finite-core Volterra components individually.
title: KLM Positivity for the Riemann Weyl Phase Kernel

description: Conjecture: For any finite number of piles, a position in Halve Nim is a P‑position (previous player winning) if and only if the bitwise XOR (nim‑sum) of the pile sizes is zero. This extends the known results for two‑pile Halve Nim and for three‑pile Halve Nim with a bounded pile to arbitrary pile numbers and sizes.
proof_strategy: Prove by induction on the total number of coins. Show that the halve move (replacing each pile ⌊p/2⌋) preserves the nim‑sum zero condition, and that from any position with non‑zero nim‑sum there exists either a standard Nim move to a zero nim‑sum position or a halve move to a zero nim‑sum position. Conversely, demonstrate that from a zero nim‑sum position every legal move (standard or halve) leads to a non‑zero nim‑sum position.
title: P-positions of Halve Nim coincide with ordinary Nim P-positions

description: For every fixed N ≥ 2 and j ≥ 2, the expected number of empty spaces E_p[U_j^N] in the j-th sibling's album at the main collector's completion time is uniquely maximized over the open probability simplex by the uniform distribution p = (1/N, ..., 1/N). Moreover, E_p[U_j^N] is Schur-concave in p, so it strictly decreases along every nonconstant ray from the uniform vector within the simplex.
proof_strategy: Express E_p[U_j^N] via the Adler–Oren–Ross integral formula, then verify the Schur-concavity of the integrand as a function of p using the Schur–Ostrowski criterion (the partial derivative monotonicity condition). Since the uniform distribution majorizes every probability vector on the simplex, Schur-concavity implies it uniquely maximizes the expectation. Uniqueness follows from strict Schur-concavity on the interior of the simplex.
title: Uniform Extremality for Siblings of the Coupon Collector

description: For sequences of block sizes $m_n$ and draw counts $k_n$ with $b_n = n - m_n \to \infty$ and $\lambda_n = n(b_n/n)^{k_n} \to \lambda \in (0, \infty)$, the number of untouched labels after $k_n$ independent uniform $m_n$-subset draws from $[n]$ converges in distribution to a Poisson($\lambda$) random variable. This captures the core coupon-collector mechanism driving the cutoff profiles for colored top-$m$-to-random shuffles.
proof_strategy: Use inclusion-exclusion to express the probability that a specific set of $r$ labels remains untouched after $k_n$ draws, showing the $r$-th factorial moment of the untouched label count converges to $\lambda^r$. This is derived by analyzing the asymptotics of $\prod_{i=0}^{r-1} \frac{b_n-i}{n-i}$ raised to the $k_n$-th power and bounding the remainder terms using the condition $\gamma_n \to 0$.
title: Poisson Limit Theorem for Variable-Block Group-Drawing

description: For every ε > 0, there exist constants δ > 0 and C > 0 (depending only on ε, not on dimension d) such that: for any d-dimensional pure simplicial complex X with two-sided local spectral expansion at most δ, every boolean function f : X(d) → {0,1} satisfying max_i Inf_i(f) ≤ ε is ε-close (in L²) to a junta on at most C faces. This conjecture asserts that the dimension dependence in the authors' Theorem 1.2 can be removed entirely for complexes with bounded local expansion, matching the dimension-independence of the classical KKL theorem on the hypercube.
proof_strategy: Either (1) refine the authors' local-to-global induction to show that the dimension accumulation across link layers telescopes to a dimension-independent constant under sufficiently strong two-sided expansion, leveraging that the λ ≤ 1/poly(d) regime permits error terms that decay exponentially in the link depth; or (2) construct an explicit family of d-dimensional HDX with λ = O(1/d) carrying boolean functions whose minimal junta approximation size grows with d, falsifying the conjecture by adapting the Kruskal-Katona shadow construction from clique complexes to complexes with tuned expansion profiles.
title: Dimension-Free KKL for Bounded-Degree HDX

description: The Petersen graph does not admit an isometric embedding into any Cayley graph of any finite abelian group. Since the Petersen graph is not a partial cube (not bipartite), it cannot embed into hypercubes Q_k = Cay((Z/2)^k, standard basis). This conjecture asserts the stronger claim that no abelian group structure whatsoever can serve as a host. The obstruction arises from the interplay between the Petersen graph's odd girth (5), vertex-transitivity under the non-abelian group S_5, and the constraint that abelian Cayley graphs impose on metric structure via their generating sets. A proof would demonstrate the limits of the paper's GF(2) quotient labeling framework and establish the Petersen graph as a minimal counterexample to isometric abelian Cayley embeddability beyond bipartite graphs.
proof_strategy: Assume for contradiction that an isometric embedding φ: Petersen → Cay(Γ, S) exists with Γ finite abelian and S symmetric generating set. Since Petersen is 3-regular, |S| = 3. Use the cycle-class parity matrix framework: the Petersen graph has 15 edges and 6 independent 5-cycles. Compute rank(A) over GF(2) and show that any edge partition yields quotient dimension incompatible with shortcut-freeness. Alternatively, exploit that Cay(Γ, S) for |Γ| ≥ 10 and abelian Γ forces commutativity constraints on the Petersen's distance-2 structure that cannot be satisfied simultaneously, using the Petersen's unique (5,2)-cage properties and odd-girth constraints on abelian Cayley quotients.
title: Petersen Graph Non-Embeddability into Abelian Cayley Graphs

description: For any integer $d \ge 1$, the maximum number of equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with common angle $\arccos(1/3)$ is bounded by $\max\{28, 2d-2\}$. This is a specific instance of Balla's conjecture, which was verified for $\alpha=1/3$ in prior work and serves as a foundational result in the theory of equiangular lines.
proof_strategy: Define the maximum number of equiangular lines $N_\alpha(d)$ in terms of the rank of the corresponding Gram matrix. Use the spectral radius order $\kappa_1=2$ to bound the multiplicity of the minimum eigenvalue of the Gram matrix, thereby deriving the $2d-2$ bound. For small dimensions $d \le 14$, use known classifications or exhaustive search to verify the absolute bound of 28.
title: Balla's Conjecture for Equiangular Lines with $\alpha = 1/3$

description: For any integer $k \ge 3$, if a multiplicative function $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfies $f(\sum_{i=1}^{2k} x_i^2) = \sum_{j=1}^k f(x_{2j-1}^2 + x_{2j}^2)$ for all positive integers $x_1, \dots, x_{2k}$, and $f(2) \neq 0$, then $f$ must be the identity function $f(n) = n$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$. This extends the paper's result for $k=3,4$ by conjecturing that the exceptional zero-tail case for $k \ge 5$ is impossible when $f(2) \neq 0$.
proof_strategy: Analyze the exceptional case for $k \ge 5$ where $f(n) = 0$ for all $n > 2k + 21$. Show that the additive condition on sums of two nonzero squares forces $f(2) = 0$ in this zero-tail scenario, yielding a contradiction. This would unify the $k \ge 3$ cases under a single identity characterization.
title: Universal Identity Characterization for Multiplicative Functions Additive on $2k$ Nonzero Squares

description: For any set of n labeled points in general position in the plane, the number of non-crossing (plane) graphs on these points is at least the number of plane graphs on n points in convex position. This formalizes the long-standing conjecture that convex position minimizes the number of plane graphs, which is supported by the paper's findings that sets with small convex hulls have significantly more plane graphs.
proof_strategy: Extend the vertex potential framework introduced in the paper to demonstrate that the expected degree plus visibility in a random plane graph is minimized when points are in convex position. Alternatively, establish a continuous deformation or edge-flip argument that monotonically increases the count of valid plane graphs as interior points are moved towards the convex hull, reducing the problem to the convex case.
title: Minimum Plane Graphs Conjecture for Convex Position

description: For each prime p, the spectral zeta function of the p-adic quantum harmonic oscillator with Hamiltonian H_p (constructed using the Vladimirov operator D_p as kinetic term on L²(ℚ_p) with quadratic potential |x|_p²) equals the local Euler factor of the Riemann zeta function at p: ζ_{H_p}(s) = Tr(|H_p|^{-s}) = (1 - p^{-s})^{-1} for Re(s) > 1. This establishes a local Hilbert-Pólya correspondence where the spectral data of a p-adic quantum system encodes the local arithmetic data of ζ(s), connecting the p-adic quantum computing framework to the spectral approach to the Riemann Hypothesis.
proof_strategy: First formalize the Vladimirov operator D_p on L²(ℚ_p) and establish its spectral properties. Then construct the p-adic Hamiltonian H_p = -½D_p + ½|x|_p² and compute its eigenvalues using p-adic eigenfunction expansions (Vladimirov's spectral theory). Show that the eigenvalue spectrum of H_p consists of groups parameterized by p-adic discs, with multiplicities given by p-adic Gaussian integrals. Compute the spectral zeta function by summing over eigenvalues grouped by p-adic valuation and identify the resulting Dirichlet series with (1-p^{-s})^{-1} via p-adic Mellin transform techniques.
title: p-Adic Quantum Harmonic Oscillator Spectral Zeta Local Euler Factor Identity

description: For a squarefree integer $D > 1$, the Blomer-Kala invariant $M_D$ of the real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ equals 1 if and only if $D = n^2 - 1$ for some integer $n \ge 2$, or $D = n^2 - 4$ for some odd integer $n \ge 3$.
proof_strategy: Define the Blomer-Kala invariant $M_D$ as a sum over complete quotients in the continued fraction expansion of $\sqrt{D}$, then prove the equivalence by showing that the sum of norms of complete quotients equals 1 precisely for $D=n^2-1$ and $D=n^2-4$.
title: Blomer-Kala Invariant One Characterization

description: For a connected graph G with rotation system σ and spanning tree T, an edge set S ⊆ E(G) defines a rotation-compatible 2-fold cover of G if and only if: (i) for every vertex v, the edges in S incident to v form a contiguous segment in the cyclic order σ_v, and (ii) for every fundamental cycle C_e of T, |S ∩ E(C_e)| is even. Condition (ii) ensures S is a cocycle (equivalently, the voltage assignment defines a valid cover), while condition (i) encodes local rotation compatibility. This conjecture provides a purely combinatorial, spanning-tree-based characterization of rotation-compatible covers, extending the structural decomposition approach of the paper.
domain_bridges: algebraic topology (covering space theory, Z₂-voltage assignments)
combinatorial graph theory (spanning trees, cycle space, cut space)
topological graph theory (rotation systems, graph embeddings)
proof_strategy: Necessity: Show any rotation-compatible 2-fold cover induces an edge set S satisfying both conditions. Condition (ii) follows because S must be a cocycle for the covering projection to be well-defined (the monodromy around every cycle must be trivial). Condition (i) follows from the definition of rotation compatibility: the local rotation at each lifted vertex must be consistent with σ_v, forcing anti-synchronous incident edges to be contiguous in the cyclic order. Sufficiency: Given S satisfying (i) and (ii), construct the 2-fold cover using T to define the fiber structure—the preimage of T is two disjoint copies since T is a tree. Condition (ii) guarantees the gluing along cotree edges is consistent, and condition (i) ensures the resulting cover is rotation-compatible.
title: Spanning Tree Characterization of Rotation-Compatible 2-Fold Covers

description: For an integer u ≥ 2, define the generalized Ankeny-Brauer-Chowla (ABC) polynomial π_u(X) = X³ - (u + u²)X² + u³X + 1 and its reciprocal polynomial X³ + u³X² - (u + u²)X - 1. Let U_n and V_n be the integer linear recurrence sequences defined by the power sums of the roots of π_u(X) and its reciprocal, respectively. While the paper proves that such sequences share at most two 'sufficiently large' common values, we conjecture that for this specific family, the total number of distinct common values is bounded by two for all integers.
proof_strategy: Establish the bound for large values using Baker's theory of linear forms in logarithms as developed in the paper, and then exhaustively verify the finiteness for the remaining range of small values using computational number theory, thereby eliminating the 'sufficiently large' caveat for this specific parametric family.
title: Finiteness of Common Values of ABC Power Sum Recurrences

description: The determinant of an \( n \times n \) matrix with entries defined by \( \binom{\ell + m - i - j + 2}{m - 1} \) for \( 1 \leq i,j \leq n \) and \( 2 \leq m \leq n \) is identically equal to 1, as shown through a bijective correspondence between lattice paths and matrix permanents.
proof_strategy: Construct a sign-reversing involution on the set of perfect matchings in a modified grid graph, where fixed points correspond to lattice paths counted by permanents of submatrices, thereby proving determinant preservation.
title: Unimodularity of Figurate Number Binomial Matrices via Bijective Proofs

description: Let ρ(q) = Σ_{n≥0} r(n)q^n be Ramanujan's third order mock theta function defined by ρ(q) = Σ_{m≥0} q^{2m(m+1)} / Π_{k=0}^{m} (1 + q^{2k+1} + q^{4k+2}). Then for all n ≥ 0: r(3n) > 0, r(3n+1) ≤ 0, and r(3n+2) ≤ 0. The paper proves the asymptotic version (for sufficiently large n) but the exact finite sign law remains open. The only zeros in the negative residue classes are r(2) = r(4) = r(8) = r(11) = r(20) = 0.
proof_strategy: The asymptotic result uses Watson's identity 2ρ(q) + ω(q) = T(q) to reduce to comparing Rademacher-type expansions for ω(q) and a theta-eta product T(q). To prove the exact finite sign law, one needs: (1) effective error bounds on the Rademacher expansion for r(n), (2) explicit computation of r(n) for all n below the effective cutoff, and (3) verification that the sign pattern holds in the finite range. The effective bound would give an explicit N₀ such that the asymptotic sign holds for n ≥ N₀; then one verifies the remaining finitely many cases computationally.
title: Exact sign law for coefficients of Ramanujan's third order mock theta function ρ(q)

description: For any integer $p \ge 2$, the classical harmonic zeta function $\zeta_H(p)$ and the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$ satisfy the identity $2\zeta_H(p) = (p+2)\zeta(p+1) - \sum_{j=1}^{p-2} \zeta(p-j)\zeta(j+1)$. This conjecture proposes the formalization of this specific classical identity, which expresses the special values of the harmonic zeta function at positive integers in terms of the Riemann zeta function.
proof_strategy: Define the harmonic zeta function and the Riemann zeta function over the reals, establish their Dirichlet series representations for convergent domains, and prove the identity using generating function techniques or by evaluating the Dirichlet convolution of the harmonic numbers and the identity sequence, reducing the sum to known telescoping properties.
title: Euler Identity for Harmonic Zeta Function Values

description: For an acyclic quiver Q of affine Dynkin type X̃ₙ where X̃ₙ ∉ {Ãₙ, Ẽ₇}, every banded coordinate projection π_{vw} (with δ_v = δ_w) surjects onto its band {(x,y) : |x−y| ≤ b_{vw}}. That is, the only non-filling banded pairs across all affine types are the source-sink diagonal in Ãₙ and the unique pair of null-root coefficient 2 vertices in Ẽ₇.
proof_strategy: Enumerate all affine types (Ṉ, D̃₄, Ẽ₆, Ẽ₈) beyond Ãₙ and Ẽ₇. For each, compute the real Schur roots via the cluster category, verify the band-existence dichotomy via null-root coefficients δ_v = δ_w, and show that for every banded pair the AR defect obstruction vanishes off-diagonal (i.e., ∂_φ ≠ e_v − e_w for all regular indecomposables φ). Use the known classification of tube ranks and regular indecomposables in each type.
title: Filling Conjecture for Banded Pairs in Affine Types Beyond Ãₙ and Ẽ₇

description: An analogue of the Colliot-Thélène conjecture for p-adic function fields: for any smooth projective rationally connected variety X over K (the function field of a smooth projective curve over a p-adic field), the unramified obstruction from H^3_nr(X, Q/Z(2)) is the only obstruction to the local-global principle, i.e., X(K) = X(A_K)^{H^3_nr}. This extends the paper's result that the unramified obstruction strictly refines the Manin obstruction, conjecturing it is in fact optimal for rationally connected varieties.
proof_strategy: Adapt the descent-theoretic strategy from the number field case: first establish that the unramified obstruction subsumes all descent obstructions from torsors under linear algebraic groups (extending Theorem 1 of the paper), then prove that for rationally connected varieties, the unramified Brauer group and higher unramified cohomology stabilize, and finally use a fibration method to reduce to lower-dimensional cases via the vanishing of H^3_nr for curves over p-adic fields.
title: Unramified Obstruction Sufficiency for Rationally Connected Varieties over p-adic Function Fields

description: Let G be a finite nilpotent group with |G|>1, and let p be the smallest prime divisor of |G|. For any integer k < p, and any two sequences a_1, ..., a_k in G (pairwise distinct) and b_1, ..., b_k in G, there exists a permutation sigma on {1, ..., k} such that the products a_1 * b_{sigma(1)}, ..., a_k * b_{sigma(k)} are pairwise distinct.
proof_strategy: Decompose the nilpotent group G into the direct product of its Sylow p-subgroups. Project the elements to the Sylow p-subgroup for the smallest prime p, and apply the paper's p-group theorem to find a permutation that makes the projected products distinct. Then, verify that this permutation (or a refined one) satisfies the distinctness condition for the full group, potentially using the abelian DKSS theorem on the remaining components.
title: Nilpotent Extension of the Feng-Sun-Xiang Theorem

description: We conjecture that for any k ≥ 2, the strong chromatic index of the odd Kneser graph O(2k-1,k) equals 2k-1. This conjecture will be used to formalize the local density inequality required for proving the affirmative answer to the first problem posed by Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Sós on maximal anti-Ramsey functions for P₄.
proof_strategy: To verify this conjecture, we will need to analyze the structure of odd Kneser graphs, their independence numbers, and apply techniques from strong chromatic index theory. Specifically, we will use the characterization of k-regular graphs with strong chromatic index 2k-1 by Lužar, Máčajová, Škoviera, and Soták. If we can show that O(2k-1,k) satisfies the necessary conditions, then it would imply that the strong chromatic index is indeed 2k-1.
title: Conjecture on Strong Edge-Colorings of Odd Kneser Graphs

description: For any normalised Hecke eigenform f of even weight k ≥ 2 for SL(2,ℤ), any positive integer j, and any even integer m ≥ 2, the Dirichlet coefficients λ_{sym^j f}(n) exhibit infinitely many sign changes as n ranges over integers representable as a sum of m squares. That is, the sets {n : n is a sum of m squares and λ_{sym^j f}(n) > 0} and {n : n is a sum of m squares and λ_{sym^j f}(n) < 0} are both infinite. This extends the paper's result (which covers 2 ≤ m ≤ 12) to all even m ≥ 2.
domain_bridges: Quadratic Forms and Sums of Squares
proof_strategy: Extend the circle method and spectral arguments from the paper's treatment of 2 ≤ m ≤ 12 to general even m ≥ 2. The key steps are: (1) establish uniform asymptotic formulas for the second moment Σ_{n≤X, n = sum of m squares} λ²_{sym^j f}(n) for all even m, using the fact that the theta series for sums of m squares is a modular form of weight m/2 for all even m; (2) derive upper bounds for the first moment Σ_{n≤X, n = sum of m squares} λ_{sym^j f}(n) that are of smaller order than the square root of the second moment; (3) combine these to conclude sign changes via the standard argument that if all coefficients had the same sign beyond some point, the first moment would be comparable to the second moment. The obstruction for large m is controlling error terms uniformly in m, which requires careful uniform estimates in the circle method setup.
title: Infinite Sign Changes of Symmetric Power L-Function Coefficients over Sums of m Squares for All Even m

description: For any normalized Hecke eigenform f of weight κ for SL(2,Z), integers j ≥ 1, k ≥ 2, h ≥ 1, q ≥ 1, and even m ∈ {2,4,6,8,10,12}, and any k-full kernel function a: ℕ → ℕ with a(n) ≪ n^ε for all ε > 0, the shifted convolution sum S(x) = ∑_{n ≤ x, n ≡ 1 (mod q), n ∈ S_m} a(n) · λ_{sym^j f}(n + h) — where S_m denotes the set of integers representable as a sum of m squares — admits an asymptotic formula S(x) = M(x) + O(x^{1-δ}) with an explicit main term M(x) satisfying M(x) ≫ x and a power-saving error term with δ > 0 depending on j, k, m, q, and h. This extends the Lü–Wang result (j = 1, k = 2) and the Venkatasubbareddy–Sankaranarayanan generalization to arbitrary symmetric power L-functions.
proof_strategy: Combine the Hecke relation λ_{sym^j f}(n) = ∑_{d|n} ψ_j(d) λ_f(n/d) for suitable coefficients ψ_j with Voronoi-type summation over sums of m squares restricted to arithmetic progressions, apply the circle method to handle the additive constraint n ≡ 1 (mod q) over S_m, use the multiplicative structure of k-full kernel functions via Dirichlet series factorization a(n) = a(a₂(n)) separating k-free and k-full parts, and invoke subconvexity bounds for L(s, sym^j f × g) over conductor ranges arising from the spectral decomposition to obtain the power-saving δ > 0.
title: Power-saving asymptotic for shifted convolution sums of symmetric power L-function coefficients against k-full kernels over sums of squares in arithmetic progressions

description: For every integer r ≥ 2, every graph H with chromatic number at least 2, and every ε > 0, there exist n₀ ∈ ℕ and δ > 0 such that for all n ≥ n₀: every n-vertex simple graph G with minimum degree δ(G) ≥ (1 − 1/(r(χ(H) − 1))) · n that is NOT (H, r)_v-Ramsey can be made r(χ(H) − 1)-partite by deleting at most εn² edges. This is the stability analogue of Observation 1.2 in the paper (which gives a Turán-type edge-density threshold for the vertex-Ramsey property), asserting that the extremal examples—complete r(χ(H)−1)-partite graphs—are essentially the only near-extremal constructions.
proof_strategy: Apply the Szemerédi regularity lemma to the reduced graph of any dense non-(H,r)_v-Ramsey graph G with δ(G) ≥ (1−1/k)n where k = r(χ(H)−1). The reduced graph inherits the non-Ramsey property and has minimum degree at least (1−1/k)|R|. By an Andrásfai-type result, the reduced graph must be close to k-partite, which pulls back to show G is close to k-partite. The key difficulty is transferring the vertex-Ramsey property through the regularity lemma, which requires careful counting lemma arguments for monochromatic copies of H in the colored partition classes.
title: Vertex-Ramsey Stability Conjecture

description:
Let B ⊂ GL(n) be a Borel subgroup and let 𝔅ₙ be the flag variety of GL(n).  There is an explicit B‑equivariant embedding ιₙ of the set of B‑orbits on 𝔅ₙ × ℙⁿ⁻¹ into the set of Borel orbits on the flag variety 𝔅_{n+1} of GL(n+1).  Each orbit in the image of ιₙ is indexed by a permutation w ∈ S_{n+1}.  The conjecture states that for any two such permutations v,w the following are equivalent:
1. The orbit ιₙ⁻¹(O_w) lies in the Zariski closure of ιₙ⁻¹(O_v).
2. v ≤ w in the Bruhat order on S_{n+1}.
This gives a complete, combinatorial description of the orbit‑closure poset on 𝔅ₙ × ℙⁿ⁻¹ and shows that the embedding ιₙ preserves the closure relations exactly as the Bruhat order does on 𝔅_{n+1}.  The conjecture is falsifiable: a counter‑example would be a pair (v,w) with v ≤ w but with ιₙ⁻¹(O_w) not contained in the closure of ιₙ⁻¹(O_v), or vice‑versa.
proof_strategy: The strategy is to first establish that the embedding ιₙ is compatible with the Demazure monoid action on the orbit set, as shown in the cited paper.  Using the known description of the Demazure product on S_{n+1} and the fact that closure relations on flag varieties are governed by the Bruhat order, one can translate the orbit closure inclusion into an inequality in the symmetric group.  A key step is to prove that the dimension of an orbit indexed by w equals the length ℓ(w) of the permutation, and that the closure of an orbit contains exactly the orbits indexed by all permutations below it in Bruhat order.  This can be carried out by induction on n, using the Gelfand–Zetlin pattern to localise the action of the stabilizer S_i and to reduce to lower rank cases.  The final step is to formalise the equivalence of the two conditions using the partial order structure in Lean, verifying the closure inclusion with dimension arguments and the Bruhat inequalities.
title: Bruhat Correspondence for Borel Orbits on 𝔅ₙ × ℙⁿ⁻¹

description: For any positive integer m, any real number p with 0 ≤ p ≤ 1/3, and any positive weights w₁,...,wₘ summing to 1, if v₁,...,vₘ are i.i.d. Bernoulli(p) random variables, then P(∑ᵢ wᵢvᵢ ≥ p) ≥ p. This is the central conjecture of the paper, which the authors connect to the Manickam-Miklós-Singhi conjecture and prove for sufficiently small p. The bound p is sharp, achieved when m=1 and w₁=1.
proof_strategy: The paper establishes a connection to the Manickam-Miklós-Singhi (MMS) conjecture. A proof might proceed by: (1) reducing to the case of rational weights via density/continuity arguments, (2) mapping the weighted Bernoulli sum problem to counting k-subsets with non-negative sum (the MMS framework), (3) leveraging the proven MMS result for n ≥ 4k to establish the bound for sufficiently small p, and (4) handling the remaining range p ∈ (ε, 1/3] through additional probabilistic or combinatorial arguments. The coupling argument of Alon et al. already handles p = 1/n.
title: Probability that a Weighted Bernoulli Sum Exceeds Its Mean is at Least p

description: For any 0 < ε < 1, there exist constants γ > 0 and C > 0 such that for any dimension n, any subset A of the discrete cube (ZMod 2)^n with |A| ≥ ε * 2^n, and any (γ, C)-well-spread set S, the Minkowski sum A + S has size at least (1 - ε) * 2^n. This generalizes the classical concentration of measure phenomenon where S is a Hamming ball.
proof_strategy: Formalize the discrete cube as (Fin n → ZMod 2), the Minkowski sum, and the definition of (γ, C)-well-spread sets (likely involving intersections with Hamming balls). Apply isoperimetric inequalities on the hypercube and properties of well-spread sets to bound the size of the Minkowski sum from below.
title: Generalized Concentration of Measure for Well-Spread Sets

description: The conjecture posits that joint descendant sizes scale asymptotically below linear growth, bounded by √n, conflicting with polynomial expectations from recursive dependencies.
proof_strategy: Convergence bounds via recursive bounds
title: Sublinear Growth of Joint Descendants

description: For any integer k ≥ 3, every [k]-graph H on n ≥ (k choose 2) + 3 vertices with δ_{k-1}(H) ≥ 1 contains a Berge-C_t^{k-1} for all k ≤ t ≤ n. This generalizes the exact bound n_0(4,3) = 9 established in the paper and the bound n_0(3,2) = 6 by Lu and Wang, positing a unified quadratic threshold for all uniformities.
proof_strategy: Induction on k, characterizing the extremal counterexamples for n < (k choose 2) + 3 using structural hypergraph theory, and applying the absorbing method to embed the Berge tight cycles for n ≥ (k choose 2) + 3.
title: Exact Threshold for Berge Tight Cycles in k-graphs

description: For a prime $q$, an integer $t \ge 1$, and a prime $p \neq q$, the congruence $\binom{q(q^t p)}{q^t p} \equiv q^{q^t p} \pmod{q^t p}$ holds if and only if $p$ divides $\binom{q^{t+1}}{q^t} - q^{q^t}$ and the base-$q$ digit sum of $(q-1)p$ is at least $(q-1)t$.
proof_strategy: The proof uses the Chinese Remainder Theorem to split the congruence modulo $q^t p$ into independent conditions modulo $p$ and modulo $q^t$. The condition modulo $p$ is derived using Lucas' theorem and Fermat's Little theorem. The condition modulo $q^t$ is established by computing the $q$-adic valuation of the binomial coefficient using Legendre's formula, which reduces the problem to bounding the base-$q$ digit sum.
title: Prime-Base Reduction for $n=q^t p$

description: For k ≥ 2 and a finite set S ⊂ ℤᵏ, let V_S = {v ∈ ℤᵏ : ∀x ∈ S, gcd(v − x) = 1} be the set of points simultaneously visible from all points in S. The autocorrelation γ_S(z) = lim_{N→∞} |V_S ∩ (V_S + z) ∩ [−N,N]ᵏ| / (2N+1)ᵏ exists for all z ∈ ℤᵏ and equals the convergent Euler product ∏_p (1 − |S_p ∪ (S−z)_p| / pᵏ), where S_p and (S−z)_p denote the images of S and S−z in (ℤ/pℤ)ᵏ respectively. This generalizes the classical single-origin visible lattice point autocorrelation (where S = {0} recovers the known formula involving the Möbius function and Riemann zeta values) to arbitrary finite observation sets, and the Euler product structure immediately implies the pure point nature of the diffraction spectrum.
proof_strategy: 1. Reformulate the visibility condition gcd(v − x) = 1 as a local condition: for all primes p, v ≢ x (mod p) in (ℤ/pℤ)ᵏ. 2. Apply the Chinese Remainder Theorem to decompose the joint condition v ∈ V_S ∩ (V_S − z) into independent conditions at each prime p: v (mod p) ∉ S_p ∪ (S−z)_p. 3. Compute each local factor as a finite counting problem in (ℤ/pℤ)ᵏ, yielding factor (1 − |S_p ∪ (S−z)_p|/pᵏ). 4. Prove convergence of the infinite Euler product using the bound |S_p ∪ (S−z)_p| ≤ 2|S| for all but finitely many p, combined with k ≥ 2 ensuring ∑_p 2|S|/pᵏ converges. 5. Rigorously justify the CRT-based density decomposition via inclusion-exclusion over primes and the uniform convergence of the partial products.
title: Euler Product for Autocorrelation of Simultaneously Visible Lattice Points

description: In the two-player average-strength team selection game with n players of strengths a_1 ≤ a_2 ≤ ... ≤ a_n and overall mean x, the parity of n completely determines which player has a non-losing strategy: if n is even, Alice (the first player/picker) has a strategy guaranteeing her team's average strength is at least x; if n is odd, Bob (the second player/picker) has a strategy guaranteeing Alice's team's average strength is at most x. This subsumes the strict winning condition: when the multiset of values with odd multiplicity is asymmetric about x, the advantaged player can guarantee a strict win.
proof_strategy: Define the game inductively as a tree of states, each tracking remaining unchosen players and current team compositions (membership lists). Define strategies as functions from game states to moves (which player to pick or which team to assign to). Prove the parity advantage by constructing explicit strategies: for even n, Alice uses a symmetric pairing strategy where she maintains a potential function based on deviations from the mean; for odd n, Bob uses a mirror strategy. The key lemma is that at each decision point, the advantaged player can make a move that preserves the invariant that their team's running sum stays at least (resp. at most) the pro-rated share of the total.
title: Average-Game Parity Advantage Theorem

description: For every non-negative integer n, the number of two-color partitions of n into distinct parts, where the smallest part occurs in exactly one prescribed color and every larger part may occur in either color or both colors, is congruent to (-1)^r modulo 4 if n is the r-th triangular number r(r+1)/2, and is congruent to 0 modulo 4 otherwise.
proof_strategy: Define the sequence s_1(n) via its generating function or combinatorial interpretation, establish the equivalence to Andrews' strictly concave compositions, and verify the congruence using the refined parity analysis and q-series expansions modulo 4.
title: Modulo 4 Characterization of Two-Color Distinct-Part Partition Coefficients

description: For every finite group G and every integer d ≥ 3, there exists a finite, simple, connected d-regular graph Γ that admits a proper d-edge-colouring κ : E(Γ) → {1,...,d} such that (1) Aut(Γ) ≅ G, and (2) κ is Aut(Γ)-invariant, meaning κ(φ(e)) = κ(e) for all φ ∈ Aut(Γ) and all e ∈ E(Γ). This strengthens Sabidussi's classical theorem (itself a strengthening of Frucht's theorem from arbitrary graphs to regular graphs) by additionally guaranteeing the existence of an automorphism-compatible edge-colouring, correcting an oversight in Sabidussi's original construction.
proof_strategy: First formalize the core graph-theoretic notions (simple graph, d-regularity, proper d-edge-colouring, automorphism group, Aut-invariance) and group-theoretic notions (finite group, group isomorphism) in Lean 4. The proof proceeds constructively: given G and d, build Γ via a modified Sabidussi-type construction (e.g., using the Cayley colour graph of G with generating set carefully chosen to ensure d-regularity, then applying a replacement operation on edges to enforce both Aut(Γ) ≅ G and the existence of an Aut-invariant proper d-edge-colouring). The key difficulty is showing the modified construction preserves Aut(Γ) ≅ G while introducing the colouring structure. A secondary approach would formalize the corrected replacement lemma that fixes Sabidussi's oversight, showing that substituting coloured gadgets for edges of the Cayley graph preserves the automorphism group.
title: Strengthened Sabidussi: Regular Graphs with Prescribed Automorphism Groups Admit Aut-Invariant Proper Edge-Colourings

description: For any natural number d, every discrete d-pseudomanifold has at least 2(d+1) vertices. This captures the fundamental extremal lower bound proven in the paper, establishing the octahedral d-sphere as the minimal such structure.
proof_strategy: Define discrete d-pseudomanifolds inductively, where a 1-pseudomanifold is defined as a cycle of length at least 4. Prove the base case for d=1 (minimum 4 vertices), and proceed by induction on d. The neighborhood of any vertex in a d-pseudomanifold forms a (d-1)-pseudomanifold, which by the inductive hypothesis has at least 2d vertices. A connectivity and regularity argument on the graph structure then bounds the total number of vertices from below by 2(d+1).
title: Minimal Vertex Bound for Discrete Pseudomanifolds

description: For every even dimension n ≥ 4, there exists a constant C > 0 such that for all odd prime powers q and all subsets E ⊆ F_q^n with |E| ≥ C·q^{n/2}, the distance set |Δ_d(E)| > (q-1)/2, where Δ_d(E) = {Σ(x_i - y_i)² : x,y ∈ E}. This asserts that the exponent n/2 (rather than n/2 + 1/3 achieved in the paper) is the true threshold guaranteeing a positive proportion of distances in even dimensions.
proof_strategy: Strengthen the Delsarte LP feasible solution construction by replacing the Kloosterman-sum-based analysis with optimal eigenvalue bounds for the association scheme of the Euclidean quadratic form in even dimensions. Alternatively, combine the LP method with Fourier-analytic incidence estimates or develop a sharp spectral gap argument for the association scheme's dual eigenvalues to eliminate the 1/3 deficit.
title: Finite Field Falconer Conjecture at the Critical Exponent for Even Dimensions

description: The sequence of log-convexity gaps $G_n = B_{n+1}B_{n-1} - (B_n)^2$ for Bell numbers is itself log-convex, meaning $G_{n+1}G_{n-1} \ge (G_n)^2$ for all $n \ge 2$.
proof_strategy: Establish that the ratio $G_{n+1}/G_n$ is monotonically increasing by leveraging the asymptotic expansion of Bell numbers alongside the explicit lower bounds for the gap provided in the paper.
title: Log-Convexity of the Bell Number Gap Sequence

description: This conjecture posits square-root cancellation for the double shifted convolution sum of Fourier coefficients of Hecke-Maass cusp forms for SL(2,Z). Specifically, for normalized Hecke-Maass cusp forms f, g, h with Fourier coefficients λ_f, λ_g, λ_h, we conjecture that for any ε > 0, the sum S(X,Y) = Σ_{1≤n≤X} Σ_{1≤m≤Y} λ_f(n) λ_g(m) λ_h(n+m) is bounded by O_{f,g,h,ε}((XY)^{1/2+ε}) whenever 1 ≤ Y ≤ X. This represents the optimal analog of the additive divisor problem for GL(2) forms and implies subconvexity for triple product L-functions.
proof_strategy: Apply the delta symbol method to separate the variables n and m, then use the spectral decomposition of the space of square-integrable automorphic forms for SL_2(Z). The main terms are controlled by the orthogonality of cusp forms, and the error terms can be bounded by applying the Kuznetsov trace formula. This ultimately reduces the conjecture to establishing the generalized Lindelöf hypothesis for the triple product L-functions L(s, f × g × h).
title: Square-Root Cancellation for Double Shifted Convolution of GL(2) Fourier Coefficients

description: The graph algebra 𝒜ₙ, whose monomial basis is indexed by simple graphs on n vertices (equivalently, the algebra of pseudo-Boolean functions on the Boolean cube {0,1}^m where m = C(n,2)), equipped with the sl₂-action defined by edge-addition and edge-deletion operators, is isomorphic as an sl₂-module to the m-th tensor power of the standard 2-dimensional sl₂-module V. Concretely, the raising operator E = Σ_{i<j} e_{ij} (adding edge {i,j}) and lowering operator F = Σ_{i<j} d_{ij} (deleting edge {i,j}) satisfy the sl₂ relations [E,F]=H, [H,E]=2E, [H,F]=-2F, and the resulting module structure on 𝒜ₙ is isomorphic to V^⊗m.
domain_bridges: Symmetric group actions on combinatorial structures
proof_strategy: Define the graph algebra 𝒜ₙ as the quotient of the polynomial ring k[x_{ij} | 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n] by the ideal (x_{ij}² - x_{ij} | 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n). Define edge-addition operators e_{ij} acting by (1 - x_{ij})· and edge-deletion operators d_{ij} acting by x_{ij}· on 𝒜ₙ. Verify the sl₂ relations for E = Σ e_{ij}, F = Σ d_{ij}, H = Σ h_{ij} where h_{ij} = e_{ij}d_{ij} - d_{ij}e_{ij}. Construct the explicit module isomorphism φ: V^⊗m → 𝒜ₙ by sending the tensor basis element ⊗_e v_e^{ε_e} to the monomial Π_{e} x_e^{ε_e}, and prove it intertwines the sl₂-actions. The key insight is that each edge position independently carries a copy of the standard sl₂-module V, with the coordinate x_{ij} tracking edge presence.
title: Graph Algebra sl₂-Module Tensor Power Isomorphism

description: Let $E$ be a $d$-dimensional Anderson $t$-module defined over a finite extension $L$ of $K=\mathbb{F}_q(\theta)$, and let $P_1, \dots, P_\ell \in E(L)$ be $L$-rational points. The $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$-module of linear relations among these points is free of finite rank. We conjecture that there exists an explicit polynomial bound on the degrees of the generators of this relation module, specifically that the maximum degree of any generator is bounded by a polynomial function in $d$, $\ell$, and the maximum of the logarithmic Weil heights of $P_1, \dots, P_\ell$. This serves as an effective analogue of Masser's relation module bounds for commutative algebraic groups.
proof_strategy: Translate the problem of finding generators for the $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$-linear relations to the existence of polynomial solutions for Frobenius difference equations, as established in the paper. Then, apply effective height bounds for polynomial solutions of such difference equations using tools from algebraic geometry over global function fields to derive the explicit polynomial degree bound.
title: Explicit Degree Bound for Generators of $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$-Linear Relations on $t$-Modules

description: Every plane triangulation on n vertices contains a P3-packing of size at least floor(n/5). This is the primary theorem for P3-packings established in the paper, proved by combining Barnette's theorem on spanning trees in 3-connected planar graphs with an inductive packing lemma on subcubic trees.
proof_strategy: First formalize Barnette's theorem to extract a spanning tree of maximum degree at most 3 from any triangulation. Then prove by induction on the number of vertices that any tree with maximum degree at most 3 contains a P3-packing of size at least floor(n/5), rooting the tree and extracting a minimal subtree of size between 3 and 5 to apply the inductive hypothesis. Finally, combine the two results to establish the bound for triangulations.
title: P3-Packing Lower Bound in Plane Triangulations

description: For every self-reciprocal (palindromic) polynomial P ∈ ℤ[X] of even degree 2m, the polynomial factors as P(x) = x^m · Q(x + x⁻¹) for a unique degree-m polynomial Q (the Chebyshev transform). All roots of P lie on the unit circle in ℂ if and only if all roots of Q are real and lie in the interval [-2, 2]. The forward direction follows because x on the unit circle implies u = x + x⁻¹ = 2Re(x) ∈ [-2, 2]; the reverse because u ∈ [-2, 2] implies both roots of x² - ux + 1 = 0 satisfy |x| = 1 since |x|² = x·x̄ = 1 when x⁻¹ = x̄.
domain_bridges: Complex modulus and unit circle geometry
proof_strategy: 1) Define self-reciprocal polynomials in Lean (coeff k = coeff (n - k)) and the Chebyshev transform Q via the identity P(x)/x^m = Q(x + 1/x), using the Chebyshev polynomial basis x^j + x^{-j} = S_j(u). 2) Prove existence and uniqueness of Q by expressing P(x)/x^m = Σ d_{m+j}(x^j + x^{-j}) + d_m = Σ d_{m+j} S_j(u) + d_m. 3) For forward direction: if |x| = 1, write x = e^{iθ}, then u = 2cos(θ) ∈ [-2,2] is real. 4) For reverse: if u ∈ [-2,2] is real, the quadratic x² - ux + 1 = 0 has roots with |x|² = 1 (discriminant u² - 4 ≤ 0 gives complex conjugate roots on the circle; u = ±2 gives x = ±1). 5) Combine multiplicity correspondence to establish the iff.
title: Chebyshev Transform Root Location Equivalence for Self-Reciprocal Polynomials

description: For every ε > 0, there exists X₀ such that for all X ≥ X₀, at least (1 - ε)⌊X/2⌋ even integers N ∈ [4, X] can be expressed as N = p₁ + p₂ with p₁, p₂ prime and p₁ - p₂ + 1 ∈ ℙ₂ (a product of at most 2 primes). This strengthens the paper's Theorem for ℙ₄ to ℙ₂, and would follow from an improved level of distribution for Goldbach primes beyond 1/6.
proof_strategy: Improve the level of distribution of Goldbach primes from θ = 1/6 to θ = 1/4 by refining the bilinear sum estimates in the minor-arc analysis, then apply the weighted sieve of Richert with the stronger level to reduce the almost-prime order from 4 to 2. The key bottleneck is bounding the Type II exponential sums with well-factorable coefficients for the Goldbach prime set.
title: Almost-Prime Goldbach Gap Conjecture

description: Let K and L be anabelomorphic p-adic fields (i.e., their absolute Galois groups Gal(K̄/K) and Gal(L̄/L) are topologically isomorphic), and let G be a connected split reductive group over Q_p. The Synchronization Conjecture (Conjecture 3.3.1 of the paper) asserts that the Fargues-Scholze local Langlands correspondence for G over K is compatible with the correspondence for G over L via the anabelomorphism. Concretely, if φ: Gal(K̄/K) → Gal(L̄/L) is a topological isomorphism, then the bijection between smooth irreducible representations of G(K) and Langlands parameters for (G, K) synchronizes with the corresponding bijection for (G, L) via the functoriality induced by φ. The author establishes this for split tori (Theorem 4.1); the conjecture extends it to all connected split reductive groups.
proof_strategy: Follow the author's strategy for split tori and extend: (1) Formalize that anabelomorphic p-adic fields yield isomorphic Langlands parameter stacks (Theorem 2.2.1), which holds because the parameter stack depends only on the absolute Galois group and the dual group Ĝ; (2) For split tori, the LLC reduces to local class field theory, which is anabelomorphically invariant by Neukirch–Uchida–Iwasawa–Ikeda theory; (3) For general reductive groups, the key obstacle is showing the excursion algebra and the central functor of Fargues-Scholze respect anabelomorphisms. A promising approach uses the geometric reformulation: show that the spectral action of the excursion algebra on ind-coherent sheaves on the stack of Langlands parameters is functorial with respect to anabelomorphisms of the base field, leveraging that Bun_G is defined purely in terms of the reductive group and the curve, while the spectral side depends only on the Galois group.
title: Anabelomorphic Synchronization of the Fargues-Scholze Local Langlands Correspondence

description: For any finite tree T with designated root r and leaf set L, if there exists a graph homomorphism f: V(T) → ℤ (satisfying |f(u) - f(v)| = 1 for all adjacent u, v) with f(v) = 0 for all v ∈ L, then for a uniformly random such homomorphism f, the variance of f(r) is at least the effective resistance R_eff(r, L) in the unit resistance network on T. This conjectures that the discrete random homomorphism variance always dominates the corresponding Gaussian (continuous) variance, which equals R_eff. Verified for paths (where Var(f(k)) ≥ k(n-k)/n on P_n) and star graphs (where Var = 1 ≥ 1/n = R_eff).
domain_bridges: Simple random walk bridges and Gaussian approximations
proof_strategy: Decompose the random homomorphism at the root into contributions from independent root-to-leaf paths. On each path, the value evolves as a discrete random walk bridge. Use a discrete-to-continuous comparison argument: the variance of a discrete random walk bridge at time k conditioned on returning to 0 at time n dominates the variance k(n-k)/n of the corresponding Brownian bridge. Apply the superposition principle for effective resistance on trees to express R_eff(r,L) as a weighted combination of path resistances, and use independence across disjoint subtrees to establish the inequality.
title: Variance-Resistance Inequality for Root Value of Random Tree Homomorphisms

description: For every n ≥ 2, the average specification number σ̄_n of Boolean threshold functions on n variables satisfies σ̄_n ≥ n + 2, strictly exceeding the minimum possible specification number n + 1. Equivalently, the average facet count of chambers in the central hyperplane arrangement dual to the lifted Boolean cube strictly exceeds n + 1. This strengthens the trivial lower bound σ̄_n ≥ n + 1 (from σ_n(f) ≥ n + 1 for all f) and complements the paper's upper bound σ̄_n ≤ 2n obtained via the Fukuda–Tamura–Tokuyama theorem.
proof_strategy: The conjecture reduces to showing that non-simplicial chambers contribute enough mass to raise the average facet count above n+1. Since σ_n(f) = n+1 exactly for simplicial chambers and > n+1 otherwise, it suffices to prove that for n ≥ 2, the proportion of threshold functions that are non-simplicial times their average excess specification number is at least 1. One approach: use the resonance arrangement connection (Section 4 of the paper) to show that the average facet count of chambers in the arrangement given by 2^n lifted cube points equals σ̄_n, then prove via the Zaslavsky-type counting or direct chamber analysis that for n ≥ 2 at least two chambers are non-simplicial with excess ≥ 1. Alternatively, use the threshold zonotope vertex-degree interpretation: the average degree of the one-inclusion graph exceeds n+1 since the graph is not complete on any regular substructure for n ≥ 2.
title: Strict lower bound on the average specification number of Boolean threshold functions

description: For every integer k ≥ 5, there exists a finite connected graph Γ such that the full reciprocal-radius polynomial P_Γ is an irreducible Salem polynomial with first sub-leading coefficient a₁ = -k. This extends the paper's sharp obstruction bound a₁ ≤ -5 by asserting realizability of every integer value in the admissible range.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit graph families realizing each coefficient value -k (k ≥ 5) by inductively modifying known Salem-realizing graphs—e.g., via suspension or vertex addition operations that increment |a₁| by one while preserving irreducibility and the Salem property—leveraging the clique-polynomial structure of P_Γ and the independence-polynomial obstructions developed in the paper.
title: Complete First-Coefficient Spectrum for Strongly Primitive Salem Growth Polynomials

description: The maximum number of unit-distance pairs among n points in the rational plane Q² is Θ(n^{4/3}). The upper bound O(n^{4/3}) follows from the Szemerédi-Trotter incidence theorem applied to unit circles in Q² (as a subset of R²). The lower bound Ω(n^{4/3}) is conjectural and supported by the algorithmic constructions in this paper, which exploit the algebraic structure of Pythagorean-type parametric families in Q² to surpass previous grid-based lower bounds. Resolving this would settle the rational analogue of the Erdős unit distance problem with matching upper and lower asymptotic exponents.
proof_strategy: The upper bound O(n^{4/3}) can be derived from Szemerédi-Trotter by viewing unit-distance pairs as incidences between points and unit circles, noting that two distinct unit circles share at most 2 points. Formalizing this in Lean requires the incidence bound for algebraic curves. The lower bound Ω(n^{4/3}) requires explicit construction of rational point families with many unit distances. The paper's algorithmic approach, based on local-breadth search over bounded rational neighborhoods rather than grid structures, provides candidate constructions. A proof would likely involve parametric families derived from the arithmetic of sums of two rational squares (generalized Pythagorean structures) and counting the resulting unit distances to establish the n^{4/3} growth rate.
title: Unit Distance Density in Q² is Θ(n^{4/3})

description: For integers $1 \le r \le n+1$, let $N(n,r)$ denote the minimum number of maximal chains in the Boolean lattice $B_n$ required to cover every strict $r$-term chain. The paper proves a general upper bound $N(n,n-t) \le n!/t$ using the inversion number of permutations modulo $t$, and shows it is exact for $t=2$. This conjecture posits the exact value $N(n,n-2) = n!/2$ for all $n \ge 2$, which is equivalent to stating that the set of permutations of $[n]$ with an even number of inversions (the alternating group $A_n$) covers all strict $(n-2)$-term chains, and no smaller set of permutations can do so.
